articles.title: Premier League: Coventry pile misery on bottom club Sunderland
articles.summary: Sunderland have not won in the league since August.
articles.content:
Premier League: Coventry pile misery on bottom club Sunderland

Sunderland have not won in the league since August.

Last Update:

Sunderland‘s miserable run in the Premier League continued as they missed a chance to move off the bottom of the table, losing 3-1 at Coventry City.

Coventry started the day just a point above the Black Cats, but took command in the first half as Tatsuhiro Sakamoto pounced on poor defending from Trai Hume to fire home his first Premier League goal before Taiwo Awoniyi doubled the lead with a deflected effort after robbing Luke O’Nien of possession.

Another deflected shot left Sunderland with a mountain to climb as Jack Rudoni’s strike was diverted home by Omar Alderete. Enzo Le Fee pulled one back from the penalty spot, but it proved nothing more than a consolation for the visitors, who had Alderete sent off in stoppage time.

While Coventry move out of the relegation zone, Sunderland remain rooted to the foot of the table with just five points from nine games, Regis Le Bris’ men without a league win since beating Fulham 1-0 back in August.

The league’s two other promoted sides shared the spoils on Humberside as Hull City drew 2-2 with Ipswich Town.

Florentino Luis gave Ipswich a deserved first-half lead, but two goals in the space of 10 minutes from Tim Iroegbunam and Oli McBurnie seemingly put the Tigers on course for the points.

However, Julio Enciso salvaged a point for Ipswich, doing so in style as he curled a long-range effort beyond Konstantinos Tzolakis.

Coventry’s win saw Nottingham Forest drop to second bottom after they were beaten 2-0 by Brentford.

Nikola Milenkovic’s own goal on the half-hour mark and Igor Thiago’s second league goal of the season sent the Bees up to sixth and ensured a fifth game without a win for Forest.

Bournemouth are just behind in seventh, the Cherries moving into the top half with a 2-0 win over Leeds United.

Leeds looked to have taken the lead in the 11th minute through Dominic Calvert-Lewin, only for his goal to be ruled out after a VAR check as he was ruled to have handled before finding the net.

And Bournemouth made the most of that let-off, Leeds goalkeeper James Trafford guilty of a horrible error as his ill-judged pass to Ao Tanaka was intercepted by Justin Kluivert, who teed up Evanilson to tap in.

Amine Adli made the points safe in injury time, producing an excellent finish from Junior Kroupi’s superb pass.

articles.title: Michael Carrick admits Man Utd problems have ‘happened too often’ after Chelsea defeat
articles.summary: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has admitted his side are making the same mistakes too often after watching them collapse in a 2-0 defeat to Chelsea at Stamford Bridge. United produced an encouraging first-half performance but failed to make their chances count before Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer struck after the break to condemn the […]
articles.content:
Michael Carrick admits Man Utd problems have ‘happened too often’ after Chelsea defeat

Last Update:

Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has admitted his side are making the same mistakes too often after watching them collapse in a 2-0 defeat to Chelsea at Stamford Bridge.

United produced an encouraging first-half performance but failed to make their chances count before Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer struck after the break to condemn the visitors to another Premier League defeat.

Carrick was particularly frustrated by how quickly the match slipped away from his players, with Lisandro Martinez’s dismissal leaving United to finish the game with 10 men.

United looked the more threatening side during the opening 45 minutes, with Matheus Cunha having a goal ruled out by VAR and several other opportunities going begging.

However, Chelsea took the lead through Rogers after the interval before Palmer converted a penalty following Martinez’s second yellow card.

Speaking to MUTV after the match, Carrick admitted United should have made more of their first-half dominance.

“Yes, that’s exactly what it was. You know it was as good as we’ve played for some time in the first half, coming here and playing that way,” he said.

“Looking so dangerous and having chances and opportunities, and we could have created more chances with the spaces that we opened up.”

The United boss acknowledged that failing to capitalise on those opportunities ultimately proved costly.

“So, going in at half-time, there’s a positive feeling but a little bit of disappointment, knowing that we hadn’t capitalised on such a good performance.”

Carrick also questioned why his side struggled to maintain their level after the restart.

“We never really got going in the second half. It started a little bit scrappy and then they score really quickly and the game changes completely after that.”

Carrick demands improvement after another Man Utd setback

The defeat adds to the pressure on Carrick, whose side have struggled for consistency during a difficult start to the campaign.

Despite finding positives in United’s first-half display, the former midfielder admitted the team’s inability to manage difficult periods has become a recurring problem.

“I think I take away a lot of the positives from the first half,” Carrick explained.

“I think we still take away, though, finding a way to let the game unravel and it get away from us. It’s happened too often really so we’ve got to learn from that and we’ve got to do something about it pretty quickly.

“We’re a great football club and we want to win football matches,” he said.

“The supporters come and, I’ve said many times, make a lot of effort, pay a lot of money to watch us play.”

articles.title: Aston Villa threaten Jamie Carragher with legal action over ‘unacceptable insults’
articles.summary: Aston Villa have announced plans for legal action against Jamie Carragher over his comments about Unai Emery.
articles.content:
Aston Villa threaten Jamie Carragher with legal action over ‘unacceptable insults’

Aston Villa have announced plans for legal action against Jamie Carragher over his comments about Unai Emery.

Last Update:

Aston Villa have announced plans to take legal action against Jamie Carragher after the former Liverpool defender claimed the club would never be as big as Manchester United.

Villa released a statement signed by chairman Nassef Sawiris accusing the Sky Sports pundit of making “unacceptable insults” towards the club and its supporters.

The dispute began after Carragher suggested Villa manager Unai Emery could be tempted to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United, with the Red Devils enduring a difficult start to the season.

The statement, signed by Sawiris, accused Carragher of disrespecting Villa and their supporters.

The club also insisted they would “not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football”.

The controversy followed Carragher’s appearance on the Stick to Football podcast, where he argued that Emery could be interested in taking charge at Old Trafford.

“Surely he would want that opportunity to manage a giant again,” Carragher said.

“There is a chain in football, whether you like it or not.”

The former England defender then compared the relationship between Villa and United to the way Real Madrid have previously signed players from the Manchester club.

“So Real Madrid will take Manchester United’s best player, they did it with [Cristiano] Ronaldo.”

Carragher went on to tell Villa supporters to “shut the f**k up”, before adding: “Aston Villa will never be Manchester United.”

Carragher responds to Villa backlash over Emery comments

Carragher has since defended his remarks, insisting his message to Villa fans was intended as a joke following criticism he had received for suggesting Emery could join United.

Speaking on the Overlap Daily, Carragher explained why he believed United should consider approaching Emery.

“I just think Unai Emery is the best manager in the league and if you’re Man Utd you’re thinking ‘what’s the best we can get?’,” he said.

“I’m not saying he’ll go – I’m just saying if it was me I’d ask the question.

“I think your own ego if someone said ‘that’s your level’ would say ‘no I’m not’. That was my point. It’s grown arms and legs.”

articles.title: Youri Tielemans backs Michael Carrick to stay at Manchester United: ‘We don’t want a sudden change’
articles.summary: Youri Tielemans insists Manchester United players want Michael Carrick to remain manager despite their poor form.
articles.content:
Youri Tielemans backs Michael Carrick to stay at Manchester United: ‘We don’t want a sudden change’

Youri Tielemans insists Manchester United players want Michael Carrick to remain manager despite their poor form.

Last Update:

Manchester United midfielder Youri Tielemans has thrown his support behind Michael Carrick, insisting the players do not want another managerial change despite the club’s disastrous start to the season.

Carrick has come under increasing pressure following consecutive defeats to Como and Bournemouth, with United enduring their worst run of results since 2015.

However, the club’s hierarchy has opted to stick with the former midfielder, who guided United back into the Champions League during his initial spell in charge last season.

Tielemans, who joined from Aston Villa in the summer, believes stability is essential if United are to turn their fortunes around.

Speaking to TNT Sports ahead of Saturday’s Premier League clash with Chelsea, Tielemans revealed that Carrick played a significant role in his decision to move to Old Trafford.

“I came here partly because of him, because he wanted me here, he wants me to help the team out,” the Belgium international said.

“So I am very happy for him to stay and the whole group, we don’t want a sudden change.

“We don’t want a big change that is going to disrupt things more than they are, we just need stability, we need to keep working hard and then it’s going to turn at some point.”

United have won just one of their opening eight Premier League matches, with a 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como followed by a 3-0 home loss to Bournemouth.

Carrick insists United players are ‘hungry’ to turn things around

Despite the speculation surrounding his future, Carrick insists his attention remains on improving performances rather than responding to criticism.

“My responsibility is the players,” he explained. “The outside is not anything for me to focus on.

“I know what we can affect, I know what we need to improve.

“The boys, I have to say, are hungry. We’re hurting because we haven’t won enough football games, but there’s an intensity, there’s a bit of an edge, there’s a disappointment, there’s a hunger to do better, for sure.”

articles.title: Pulisic gets his wish as USA star pens new Milan deal until 2031
articles.summary: Pulisic's deal was announced on the eve of Milan's derby with Inter.
articles.content:
Pulisic gets his wish as USA star pens new Milan deal until 2031

Pulisic's deal was announced on the eve of Milan's derby with Inter.

Last Update:

Christian Pulisic said it was always his wish to remain with AC Milan after signing a new contract with the club.

The United States forward’s contract was due to expire at the end of the current campaign, though it featured an option for a further year.

But Milan confirmed on Friday that Pulisic had penned fresh terms on the eve of their derby with leaders Inter Milan.

Speaking to Sky Sport Italia after signing his deal, Pulisic said: “Incredible, I’m really excited, it was always my wish to stay here, to renew here with Milan and I’m really excited for the next few years.

“I always wanted Milan. All the confidence that Milan have put in me from top to bottom has always been top and I’m really happy here.”

Pulisic joined Milan in 2023 after an unsuccessful spell at Chelsea.

He has made 142 appearances for the Rossoneri, scoring 44 goals and providing 25 assists.

The 28-year-old has two goals to his name already this season and will look to add to his tally in the Derby della Madonnina, which Milan enter seven points behind defending champions Inter.

articles.title: Chelsea fear Maxence Lacroix could miss 10 games as Xabi Alonso confirms injury blow
articles.summary: Chelsea fear Maxence Lacroix could be sidelined until January with a serious hamstring injury as Xabi Alonso provides an update ahead of Manchester United.
articles.content:
Chelsea fear Maxence Lacroix could miss 10 games as Xabi Alonso confirms injury blow

Chelsea fear Maxence Lacroix could be sidelined until January with a serious hamstring injury as Xabi Alonso provides an update ahead of Manchester United.

Last Update:

Chelsea fear defender Maxence Lacroix could be sidelined until January after suffering a serious hamstring injury during their Carabao Cup defeat to Liverpool.

The France international, who joined the Blues from Crystal Palace for £52million in the summer, could miss up to 10 matches after picking up the problem during Wednesday’s penalty shootout defeat.

Manager Xabi Alonso has confirmed Lacroix will be unavailable until at least after the international break, although reports suggest his absence could extend considerably longer.

Lacroix sustained the injury towards the end of the first half against Liverpool while sprinting to block a shot.

The 26-year-old has been a regular under Alonso this season, starting all but one of Chelsea’s 11 matches across all competitions.

Only Morgan Rogers has played more minutes for the Blues, making his potential absence a significant setback ahead of a busy period.

Asked about the defender’s condition before Saturday’s Premier League clash with Manchester United, Alonso said: “Max, he picked up an injury, and we expect that he’s not going to be ready before the international break. So he will be a few weeks out.”

Chelsea boss discusses defensive replacements ahead of Man Utd clash

Alonso must now consider his alternatives at centre-back, with Jorrel Hato and Aaron Anselmino also currently unavailable through injury.

Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill and Josh Acheampong are among the options available to the Chelsea manager.

“With Max’s injury, we have Wes, we have Levi [Colwill], Josh [Acheampong], he could play as well as centre-back,” Alonso explained.

“Jorrel when he is back with the team [is an option]. Wes has played [and] even if he missed the penalty [in the shootout], I think that he had a good game.

“He was consistent, he was strong and I saw many positives from his performance. We know the level that he has had and he’s going to be important.”

Alonso also confirmed goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez is having a protective mask fitted as he recovers from a broken jaw.

articles.title: Maresca insists no Man City player is undroppable after Donnarumma’s Villa horror show
articles.summary: Maresca said his XI for City's league game with Brighton would be "Gigio plus 10".
articles.content:
Maresca insists no Man City player is undroppable after Donnarumma’s Villa horror show

Maresca said his XI for City's league game with Brighton would be "Gigio plus 10".

Last Update:

Enzo Maresca has made it clear no members of his Manchester City side are undroppable despite a public show of support for goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Donnarumma was culpable for both goals as City lost 2-1 to Aston Villa last Saturday, and was subsequently rested as Maresca’s men beat Brighton and Hove Albion in a penalty shootout to progress to the quarter-finals of the EFL Cup.

Gerónimo Rulli made two penalty saves to help secure City’s progression, but Maresca confirmed immediately thereafter that the team for Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Brighton would be “Gigio plus 10”.

Pressed on those comments in his pre-match press conference, Maresca said: “I think it is one thing to say that at his moment it is Gigio plus 10, and another thing to say he is undroppable.

“They are two different things. There is no player who is undroppable but there is a moment where it is Gigio plus ten because in this moment I see it like this.

“Any player makes mistakes, [what is] important is to move on, understand the reason why, to learn from that mistake and move on. In this moment we are talking about Gigio but remember the last minutes the save at Manchester United away.

“All players make mistakes at some point of the season, sometimes it costs points and sometimes not because we are lucky but I think it’s a normal process from Gigio.”

Maresca confirmed that Antoine Semenyo is the only City player unavailable for the game as he continues his rehabilitation from a knee injury.

“They are all available,” he said at his press conference “[Apart from] Antoine Semenyo, the rest are all available.”

“He’s [Semenyo] good. He’s in a good mood. He’s in the building making the recovery sessions and the therapy that he needs but it’s too early for now.”

articles.title: Andoni Iraola reveals key to beating Arsenal as Liverpool boss targets fourth win in five meetings
articles.summary: Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola warns his side cannot repeat his Bournemouth tactics against Arsenal despite winning three of his last four meetings.
articles.content:
Andoni Iraola reveals key to beating Arsenal as Liverpool boss targets fourth win in five meetings

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola warns his side cannot repeat his Bournemouth tactics against Arsenal despite winning three of his last four meetings.

Last Update:

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has warned his players that they cannot rely on his previous success against Arsenal when the two Premier League sides meet at Anfield on Sunday.

The Spaniard has beaten the Gunners in three of his last four meetings with them as a manager, having enjoyed an impressive record against Mikel Arteta’s side during his time at Bournemouth.

However, Iraola insists those results will count for little this weekend, with Liverpool requiring a different approach to overcome their title rivals.

Speaking ahead of Sunday’s meeting, Iraola acknowledged his previous success against Arsenal but stressed that Liverpool present a completely different challenge.

“It is true that I do have good results with Bournemouth against them but this doesn’t mean a lot,” he said.

“This is a totally different team, a different group of players in a different moment. We cannot use the same things we used with Bournemouth against Arsenal.

“We have to use different tools, use our players as good as we can and trust them.”

Liverpool boss identifies key to beating Arsenal

Iraola also outlined the areas where Liverpool must compete if they are to get the better of Arsenal, highlighting the importance of physical battles and set-pieces.

“At the end it is going to be a matter of winning the duels, running more than them, winning the set-play mini-games and these sort of things you have to control against Arsenal.”

His comments suggest Liverpool will need to match Arsenal’s intensity across the pitch, with the outcome potentially hinging on fine margins rather than any particular tactical advantage.

The meeting represents another significant test for Iraola as he looks to build on Liverpool’s recent performances and improve their Premier League form.

Having already shown he can find ways to beat Arsenal, the former Bournemouth boss will now be hoping to achieve the same result with a different group of players.

articles.title: Chelsea: Man United struggles will not alter Alonso approach as he expresses ‘great sympathy’ for Carrick
articles.summary: Carrick will look to improve United's fortunes against a Chelsea side that has suffered a dip in form.
articles.content:
Chelsea: Man United struggles will not alter Alonso approach as he expresses ‘great sympathy’ for Carrick

Carrick will look to improve United's fortunes against a Chelsea side that has suffered a dip in form.

Last Update:

Xabi Alonso has “great sympathy” for Michael Carrick but insisted the situation around the under-pressure Manchester United manager will not impact Chelsea‘s approach to their Premier League fixture with the Red Devils on Saturday.

Carrick is under huge scrutiny following United’s dismal start to his first season as manager after a successful interim spell last term.

United have taken just seven points from their opening eight Premier League games, leaving them 16th and just a point above the relegation zone. They are out of the EFL Cup and have lost two of their opening three Champions League games.

Yet Carrick has been given the chance to turn their fortunes around despite talk United have already discussed potential successors.

The home fans at Old Trafford were vocal in their support for Carrick following their 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth last Sunday.

Bruno Fernandes was left on the bench for that game having questioned Carrick’s tactics in their 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como, and supporters sang Carrick’s name as he went down the tunnel, before making their feelings clear by immediately then booing the players.

Fernandes and Carrick have since held clear-the-air talks as United aim to get things back on track, though a trip to Stamford Bridge represents another difficult test.

Chelsea are in a much healthier position under Alonso, sitting fifth with 13 points, but are themselves looking to rediscover a winning feeling after following up a 2-0 loss to Tottenham by going out of the EFL Cup with a penalty shootout defeat to Liverpool.

And Alonso is not focused on the drama around United as he looks to lead his team to a bounce-back win.

“I have great respect, I have great sympathy for Michael as a manager,” Alonso told a pre-match press conference.

“I know him because we have played against each other. We played recently in a legends game and we had a little chat. He is a good guy and one you want to be around. Aside from that, it is not for me to comment.”

Asked if the issues at United alter Chelsea’s attitude to the game, he replied: “For me, it doesn’t change. We need to prepare the same way.

“We can only control what we can control. We know they are a good team, it doesn’t matter about the table. They have a good squad, good player, good manager.

“We are back in Premier League mode and that for me is the main competition for us – this year and almost every year.

“It is a big one. We didn’t have long to prepare but it’s really important after the last home game we had that we keep winning games and get that winning feeling.

“As soon as we left Liverpool, we were thinking about United. I saw a better version of us on Wednesday than I did on Saturday, even though the result wasn’t what we wanted in either. This is a journey where we will have tough moments and we need to learn from them.”

articles.title: De Zerbi warns Tottenham must avoid ‘taking risks’ with injuries but Maddison available after Chelsea knock
articles.summary: Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi has confirmed James Maddison is available for selection after picking up a knock against Chelsea.
articles.content:
De Zerbi warns Tottenham must avoid ‘taking risks’ with injuries but Maddison available after Chelsea knock

Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi has confirmed James Maddison is available for selection after picking up a knock against Chelsea.

Last Update:

Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi has confirmed James Maddison is available for selection but warned that Spurs must be careful not to rush players back from injury.

The midfielder has been working his way back to full fitness after recovering from an ACL injury, but suffered a groin strain in the 2-0 win over Chelsea last week.

However, Tottenham remain without Tosin Adarabioyo, Lucas Bergvall and Mykhailo Mudryk, who are all sidelined.

Speaking ahead of Tottenham’s clash with Crystal Palace, De Zerbi delivered a positive update on Maddison’s fitness while confirming three other players remain unavailable.

“James Maddison is available. Tosin is still out, [so are] Bergvall and Mudryk, but everyone else is available.”

Asked whether Maddison could get away with training less than his team-mates, the Italian stressed the importance of hard work and maintaining fitness.

“I believe in working. I come from a city, Brescia [where] we are used to working hard and we believe in working in hard you receive the good back,” he said.

“For James Maddison or any player coming back from injury, [you] have to work more than the other players but he’s already working hard for four, five weeks and consistently.”

Tottenham boss explains injury concerns after Porro and Kulusevski setbacks

De Zerbi also discussed the importance of managing players carefully, particularly after previous injury problems involving Pedro Porro and Dejan Kulusevski.

The Spurs boss suggested that missing a couple of training sessions is not necessarily a concern, provided the club makes sensible decisions about a player’s fitness.

“So it’s not a problem if you miss two days and then we have to analyse if we take risks or not,” he explained.

“Because if we take risks like we did with Pedro Porro and [Dejan] Kulusevski… we are lucky to have a big squad [but] it’s [about] not taking risks for new injuries.”

articles.title: Hansi Flick makes feelings on Barcelona clear following Clasico defeat
articles.summary: Barca are looking to bounce back after successive defeats.
articles.content:
Hansi Flick makes feelings on Barcelona clear following Clasico defeat

Barca are looking to bounce back after successive defeats.

Last Update:

Hansi Flick made it clear he retains complete confidence in his Barcelona team and that he has the support of the club’s board following their Clasico defeat to Real Madrid.

Barca suffered successive high-profile defeats last week as they followed a 4-2 loss to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League by losing the Clasico at home to a pair of Kylian Mbappe goals.

Mbappe gave Jose Mourinho’s men the lead in the 41st minute at Camp Nou, before Raphinha restored parity just after the hour mark.

But it was Mbappe who had the final say, the France star presented with a simple finish after superb work in the final third from Eduardo Camavinga.

Barcelona are two points clear of Atletico Madrid at the top of LaLiga as they look to defend their title, with Madrid just a point further back.

However, Flick is not feeling the pressure from sporting director Deco or president Joan Laporta.

Speaking ahead of Saturday’s clash with Alaves, Flick said: “I spoke with the president and Deco. It’s great. I know the situation.

“We’ve lost two games in a week, but I have complete confidence in my team. Nothing has changed. I don’t see any lack of mentality. I’m very happy to be here. Nothing has changed.

“We won the first 11 games, now we’ve lost two, and we have to get back to winning ways. That’s our job.

“I’m totally convinced of our style of play. We’ll stick with it until the end. That’s the most important thing, to be convinced of our approach.”

Barca are dealing with several injuries in defence, with centre-backs Andreas Christensen and Eric Garcia unavailable, along with full-backs Jules Kounde and Xavi Espart.

Asked about speculation of Barca pursuing a centre-back in the transfer window, Flick replied: “I said it during the transfer window, we always talk about what’s best for the team, how we can improve it.

“It’s something we’re working on. We’ll see. We have a few weeks left before the transfer window opens,” he said.

“We’ve discussed it with Deco, [football coordinator] Bojan , and my staff. That’s how we do things. If we can, maybe we will.

“Defending isn’t just a job for the defenders; everyone is involved. First, we can’t afford to lose possession easily like we did against Real Madrid. It’s not good. It’s not the quality we usually have. I already said that perhaps we weren’t very fresh.

“We need to play with more concentration. And when it’s time to defend in the box, it’s important to mark the opponent. We weren’t very good at that. We have to improve. We’re training this and talking to the players about it. We have to manage it.

“We need to control matches, have more possession, and fewer turnovers. That’s the key. You have to decide how to move the ball and the opponent. It’s good not to lose possession, otherwise you have to chase it.

“We need to improve on this. The way forward is to make fewer mistakes. We need to stay calm and play with more control.”

articles.title: We are not in Disneyland – Arsenal boss Arteta delivers x-rated response to Dowman red card
articles.summary: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta remains angry at Max Dowman's red card at Fleetwood on Tuesday night
articles.content:
We are not in Disneyland – Arsenal boss Arteta delivers x-rated response to Dowman red card

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta remains angry at Max Dowman's red card at Fleetwood on Tuesday night

Last Update:

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has rubbished suggestions he was too harsh on Max Dowman following his red card at Fleetwood on Tuesday night.

Dowman, 16, was sent off for a kick out at Harrison Neal following a bruising tackle in the 85th minute of the EFL Cup tie. Fleetwood went on to complete a huge shock by winning the penalty shoot-out.

Arteta directed some angry words at Dowman when he walked off the field at Highbury Stadium and has been criticised for not taking a softer approach with the youngster.

However, he doubled down on his actions today, suggesting Dowman needs to learn quickly to avoid a repeat.

“We are not in Disneyland, we’re in the Premier League,” said Arteta, whose second-placed side visit Liverpool on Sunday.

“If you see the reaction from my mother and father with me sometimes, you’d say ‘you don’t like that reaction’ but for me it was the best reaction ever as it enabled me to be who I am.

“What do you expect? That’s the level and that’s the reaction. Whether it’s right or wrong, that’s the reaction. And the reaction when I don’t win, I’m p***** off, big time. This is the environment and the reality.”

Arteta spoke with Arsenal starlet Dowman yesterday

He added: “My reaction comes in a moment of heat and extreme frustration because I know the consequences of that, especially for Max. We discussed it just before we went out and it will continue to happen unfortunately because of how he attracts opponents.

“He’s 16 and we have to be very protective of him but also very straight with what we expect from him towards the team, individual and the club.

“I had a talk with him yesterday. There are no issues at all. I’ve done it. That’s why I’m so protective of these things and young players as we have all made these mistakes.

“We know how much you can get punished. And what happens next. It’s not the first time, it happened earlier this month with England, so we need to put an end to it very quickly.”

Dowman appeal rejected with Arsenal ‘very disappointed’

Arsenal appealed the red card but that has been rejected, meaning the winger will miss the next three games.

Arteta added: “Very disappointed to be fair, especially with the reckless tackles he received. His reaction is minimum in relation to the action. I’m disappointed that it has not been overturned.”

“It is what it is. We have put every argument on the table to make a case for it. The action is so evident. Obviously we have a very different opinion and on top of that I think you have to read the context of the player, the age and what happened previously.

“It could have been really bad. We are lucky today that he hasn’t had a broken foot, that is clear.”

Dowman would have been in the Arsenal squad for the trip to Anfield with Bukayo Saka injured and Noni Madueke a doubt.

Arteta said Madueke was not yet ruled out and also confirmed Declan Rice, Christos Tzolis and Riccardo Calafiori would be involved if they come through Saturday’s training session unscathed.

articles.title: San Siro replacement needed to bridge gap to European elite, insists Inter Milan president Marotta
articles.summary: AC MIlan and Inter Milan expect to move into a new home in 2031.
articles.content:
San Siro replacement needed to bridge gap to European elite, insists Inter Milan president Marotta

AC MIlan and Inter Milan expect to move into a new home in 2031.

Last Update:

Inter Milan president Beppe Marotta believes the replacement for San Siro is crucial to help them bridge the financial gap to their rivals in European football.

The Nerazzurri and rivals AC Milan, who have shared the iconic San Siro since 1947, on Thursday unveiled plans to replace it with a new home that would be called the Generali Stadium for 20 years.

As part of the plans, San Siro would be demolished. Work on the Generali, which will be built adjacent to the site of San Siro, will begin in 2028, with the stadium is expected to be ready for the 2031-32 campaign. Milan and Inter will continue to play at San Siro until the Generali is ready.

While the plan to demolish San Siro has been a source of controversy, Marotta believes the move is necessary for Inter to be able to compete at the highest level.

“In some respects, whilst San Siro represents a repository of historical memory, it no longer meets the requirements of a modern stadium or what the fans want,” Marotta told The Athletic.

“Just consider that, according to the figures we have today, Real Madrid generates around €250m a year [from the Bernabeu], whilst we’re currently just under €100m with San Siro. As well as being an asset for the club, a stadium is also a source of revenue.

“At present, there’s far too big a gap between us in Italy and some of our rival clubs in Europe, which also affects our competitiveness and certainly puts us in a very difficult position.

“A stadium must have a life of its own and be functional, not just on Sundays or when matches are played.”

The new stadium is being made possible in large part due to private capital from the United States, with Milan’s owners Red Bird and Inter’s owners Oaktree Capital Management collaborating on the project.

“In Italy, where there are major bureaucratic hurdles to launching projects of this nature, this has come about thanks in part to the arrival and tenacity of Oaktree,” Marotta added.

“Their tenacity has perhaps broken down some of the bureaucratic barriers which, in our country, unfortunately represented a major stumbling block and were difficult to overcome. Today, we are truly on an upward trajectory.”

Milan and Inter meet Derby della Madonnina on Saturday. Inter are top of Serie A as they look to defend the Scudetto, the Nerazzurri ahead of Lazio on goals scored. Milan are seven points off the pace.

Manchester United set to be snubbed in surprise move for Leeds striker Calvert-Lewin

Manchester United's surprise move for Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin is set to end in disappointment

Last Update:

Manchester United are set to miss out on a surprise January target with Dominic Calvert-Lewin on the verge of signing a new contract at Leeds.

United were reported to be interested in the 29-year-old after being impressed at the way he has rebuilt his career at Elland Road since moving from Everton in 2025.

Calvert-Lewin crossed the Pennines 16 months ago on a free transfer having struggled with numerous injury problems that restricted him to just 92 Premier League appearances in his final four seasons with the Toffees.

Leeds, then newly promoted, took a chance on him and have been richly rewarded. Calvert-Lewin scored 14 league goals in 35 appearance last season and already has four in eight this term, including one against Manchester United two weeks ago in a 1-1 draw.

More importantly, he has stayed fit having changed his routines and improved his nutrition, recovery and sleep patterns.

United target Calvert-Lewin back in the England fold

Calvert-Lewin was recalled by England in March and, although he missed out on a place at the World Cup, he won his 14th cap last month in the 3-0 win over Czechia.

He had been linked with United as they search for experienced cover for Benjamin Sesko. Calvert-Lewin’s current deal expires in 2028 but reports this morning suggest he is ready to commit his long-term future to the West Yorkshire club.

Sesko has been ruled out until January at least due to a shin injury, leaving Michael Carrick short of an out-and-out number nine to lead the line. They have been operating with Matheus Cunha or Bryant Mbeumo in attack but both men prefer to play in a slightly more withdrawn role.

United go to Chelsea on Saturday lunchtime with Carrick’s job hanging by a thread. The 3-0 loss to Bournemouth last Sunday was their eighth game without a win in all competitions and they go into the weekend in 16th place in the Premier League table.

Captain Bruno Fernandes will return at Stamford Bridge after conciliatory talks with Carrick this week. The Portugal international was benched last weekend for criticising the head coach’s tactics in the Champions League defeat to Como.

articles.title: AC Milan and Inter unveil 71,500-seater ‘Generali Stadium’ to replace San Siro
articles.summary: The Serie A giants reveal joint plans for their state-of-the-art new home
articles.content:
AC Milan and Inter unveil 71,500-seater ‘Generali Stadium’ to replace San Siro

The Serie A giants reveal joint plans for their state-of-the-art new home

Last Update:

AC Milan and Inter have officially taken the wraps off the design for their proposed new home: the Generali Stadium.

The joint venture will see the two historic Milanese rivals swap the legendary San Siro for a modern 71,500-capacity venue.

Designed by the architects originally behind the new Wembley Stadium the ground will sit at the heart of a 281,000-square-metre urban regeneration project in the San Siro district.

Italian insurance and asset management giant Generali has secured the long-term naming rights in what the clubs described as one of the largest sponsorship deals of its kind in global sport.

The venue’s standout architectural feature is an exposed concrete X-frame supporting a double-curved roof. Inside, the design aims to replicate the ferocious atmosphere of the existing San Siro, featuring two continuous 360-degree tiers and steep stands banked at angles of up to 37 degrees to pull supporters as close to the pitch as possible.

The clubs hope the modern commercial infrastructure will finally close the financial gap on Europe’s elite.

Construction is scheduled to get under way in 2028, with the clubs targeting an official opening match in time for the 2031/32 season, subject to final planning approvals.

Italy – and the new stadium – are scheduled to host Euro 2032.

Manchester United boss Carrick talks Bruno Fernandes ‘decision’

Bruno Fernandes could return for Man United at Chelsea

Last Update:

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick says Bruno Fernandes is “fully committed” after remaining an unused substitute for the home defeat to Bournemouth on Sunday following the captain’s public criticism of the Premier League strugglers’ tactics.

The reigning Premier League Player of the Season said the decision not to press Como man-for-man in United’s 4-1 away defeat in the Champions League last Wednesday was “on the manager and staff”, leading to the Portugal playmaker moving to the bench for the 3-0 thrashing by the Cherries in the Premier League.

“It was a decision for what we felt for the game,” said Carrick, who was widely reported to have held clear-the-air talks with his star player on Tuesday.

“That’s it. Bruno’s fully committed to this football club. I’ve got absolutely no issues with that. We move forward and make decisions as we go.”

Manchester United: Will Bruno Fernandes play vs Chelsea?

Should Carrick and Bruno Fernandes have resolved the situation, the 32-year-old could return to the starting line-up for United’s trip to Chelsea on Saturday (12:30 GMT).

“I have to say, the boys are hungry,” suggested Carrick, adding that his squad are “looking forward” to attempting to end their eight-match winless run in all competitions against opponents who are six points above them.

“There’s an intensity, a bit of an edge, a disappointment and a hunger to do better.”

Michael Carrick news: Will United sack manager?

United director of football Jason Wilcox is said to have decided that Carrick will be given more time despite his side’s dreadful form in the former Red Devils midfielder’s first full season in charge.

Carrick, who made United the form team in the top flight and guided them to Champions League qualification after being appointed on an initial interim basis in January, reiterated that he has not been considering his position.

“I really don’t need any assurances from anyone,” said the 45-year-old, whose exit is considered a formality by many fans and pundits.

“I understand the job, the responsibilities and what comes with that. I care about what the supporters think. I care about what it feels like in the stadium and travelling for games.

“I care about what we give them and what they see. I genuinely don’t take any notice of anything else. I know this job, I know what it brings and what we need to do to be better. I don’t need anyone else to tell me.”

articles.summary: Lionel Messi was a peripheral figure as Inter Miami were held to a 2-2 draw by FC Cincinnati on Wednesday
articles.content:
Subdued Messi fails to fire as Fillipi salvages draw for Inter Miami

Lionel Messi was a peripheral figure as Inter Miami were held to a 2-2 draw by FC Cincinnati on Wednesday

Last Update:

Riquelme Fillipi scored a brilliant 90th-minute equaliser to salvage a point for Inter Miami in a 2-2 draw with FC Cincinnati that damages the Floridians’ hopes of securing second spot in the Eastern Conference.

Fillipi’s first MLS goal helped Miami avoid just their seventh league defeat of the season but they still slipped to third after the New England Revolution beat the New York Red Bulls 3-2.

Miami visit New England on Sunday.

Luis Suarez gave Miami the lead just after the hour mark with a trademark curling strike but Miami then sat back, allowing the visitors to get a grip on the game and goals from Kenji Mboma Dem and Samuel Gidi swung the match in their favour.

Filippi levelled but Miami still needed a brave block from defender Ian Fray to deny Evander in stoppage time.

“What I know is that we made mistakes again, I think, in part, due to a great deal of anxiety, especially in the second half,” Miami boss Kily Gonzalez said.

“In my view, we were far too passive in the first half, which is something we tried to address at halftime. I’ll say it again: our fate is in our own hands – we need to win a match – but we have to improve significantly.

“We need to better analyse and interpret the game and understand how it should be played. We need to be more aggressive, and in the first half, we simply weren’t.”

Messi on the periphery but collects yellow card

Lionel Messi returned to the starting line-up but had a quiet night, bar picking up a yellow card for a clash with Cincinnati defender Samuel Gidi.

His struggles were indicative of a strangely ineffective performance from Miami.

“The match demanded a lot of individual duels, one-on-one situations, and play out on the flanks,” González added. “We needed to be clinical, but we lacked the sharpness to execute what we had prepared during the week. So, yes, we’re very frustrated, but we have to keep going.”

Cincinnati stay in eighth place in the East and very much in play-off contention.

articles.content:
Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko ruled out until January to add to Carrick’s woes

Sesko has not started in the Premier League this season

Last Update:

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has been dealt another headache after Benjamin Sesko was ruled out until January with a shin injury, according to The Athletic.

Sesko last played on September 16 when he started the Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton. A week later United released a statement saying: “Benjamin will undergo tests this week before defining his individual recovery plan.”

United have made a dreadful start to the season, with Carrick still in charge despite immense pressure coming his way. After public rifts with both captain Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martinez, this will add to his issues.

The Slovenia has come off the bench to feature in United’s first four Premier League games of the season, starting only once in the Champions League against Sabah as well as the cup outing versus Brighton.

Athletic report: Sesko played through pain

The report claims the issue first developed last season, when the 23-year-old continued playing during the final two months of the campaign despite feeling discomfort.

United opted to rest the £74million striker rather than send him for surgery, causing him to miss pre-season.

The same issue has now occured, so the Red Devils are opting to rest him until the new year in the hope that he will avoid a setback when he eventually returns.

Sesko was a regular presence at Carrington throughout June and pushed to return in August, coming off the bench in United’s opening game against Hull City.

Sesko injuries since Man Utd move

Injuries have rarely been a problem throughout his career, making his current spell on the sidelines particularly unusual. In just 14 months at United, Sesko has missed more than twice as many days through injury as he did during his entire two-year spell at RB Leipzig.

The striker takes a meticulous approach to his fitness, practising yoga daily and having access to a private gym, ice bath, swimming pool and sauna at home.

Sesko scored 12 goals for United last season and has made a promising start to the current campaign, finding the net twice in six appearances.

articles.content:
Real Madrid apologise for Mbappe gaffe and express ‘deep respect for China’

Real Madrid have apologised to the Chinese people following Kylian Mbappe's remarks about the country's former leader Mao Zedong

Last Update:

Real Madrid have issued an official apology to the Chinese people as the row over Kylian Mbappe’s ill-judged remarks regarding Mao Zedong shows no sign of abating.

Mbappe said sorry on Tuesday after suggesting he found a meme that superimposed his face on to “some guy – I think he’s a Chinese dictator” funny. The meme in question featured Mao, the country’s founding leader who died in 1976. Mao’s policies are widely blamed for mass starvation and millions of deaths but it is still taboo in China to mock a historical figure of his prominence.

There have been reports Chinese state television have suspended broadcasts of La Liga matches in protest and Real Madrid moved on Wednesday to offer their apologies.

A club statement read: “Real Madrid wishes to express its apologies to the Chinese people for any discomfort that may have been caused by the recent words of our player Kylian Mbappé.

“Our club holds deep respect for China, its history, its culture, and its citizens, as well as for the millions of Chinese fans who feel affection and admiration for Real Madrid.

“The club joins the public apology expressed by Kylian Mbappé, in which the player himself has conveyed his regret for his words and reiterated his respect for the Chinese people.

“Real Madrid reaffirms its commitment to the values of respect, coexistence, and understanding among cultures, and expresses its desire to continue strengthening the bonds of friendship and affection that unite it with China and its citizens.”

Kylian Mbappe: Full apology to people in China

Mbappe, who made the remarks on YouTube show The Bridge hosted by Blancos team-mate Aurelien Tchouameni, showed remorse for his words on Tuesday.

“During a recent interview, I reacted to an image featuring myself,” said Mbappe. “My comment was ill-judged and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world.

“I apologise to everyone my words have upset. That was absolutely not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history and I am sincerely sorry.”

What is Kylian Mbappe alleged to have said about China?

In unverified clips online, Mbappe does not name Mao but says he uses the meme “all the time” with friends, adding that it “makes me laugh the most… there’s a video of a guy, I think it’s a Chinese dictator…”

Chinese football forum Dongqiudi reportedly highlighted the interview, calling it “inappropriate” and liable to “hurt the feelings of Chinese people”.

Mao is an icon of the Communist Party in China, where the internet and digital content are subject to strict state control and the former leader is one of the most closely regulated topics.

The original video is not on The Bridge’s YouTube channel and it is unclear when the episode first aired. Mbappe spoke in September about memes depicting him as a dictator, which is his apparent nickname in the Madrid dressing room. “Part of it is funny because you get the sense that, for some people, it’s all in good fun,” he told L’Equipe.

“There’s also a less funny part because we know the damage these kinds of people have caused throughout history.

“To be compared to people who murder others, or who have made millions and millions of people unhappy… I don’t think I’ve ever done anything like that in my life.

“So there’s a mix of things. On the one hand, I know it’s done in a light-hearted way and doesn’t go that far, but it sometimes shows a lack of political and human awareness in people.”

Kylian Mbappe: Full La Liga statement

La Liga said it “deeply regrets the offence caused” to Chinese fans. “These comments were made in a personal capacity and do not represent La Liga,” it added.

“To the extent of our institutional responsibility, we apologize on behalf of La Liga and all its clubs.

“Spanish football upholds respect, coexistence, and unity among people of all cultures. We convey our respect to China, its institutions and its people and we deeply value the support of the millions of fans who follow us each week.

“We reaffirm our commitment to a relationship built over years. We are working with our partners and institutional interlocutors in China to address this situation.

“Likewise, in collaboration with the clubs and players, we will implement a protocol for awareness and communication that promotes respect for different cultures and helps prevent similar situations.”

Kylian Mbappe: What has the reaction been in China?

On Tuesday morning, four topics related to Mbappe remained among the top 10 trending searches on China’s social media platform, Weibo, Reuters reported.

The report said some internet critics had called ​for China to blacklist Mbappe and “reduce his commercial value to zero”, receiving hundreds of likes in response.

Reuters cited a spokesperson for China’s Foreign Ministry as saying that words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people “will naturally be met with joint opposition from all sectors of Chinese society.”

Confirmed Chinese brands to have dropped Mbappe

The country’s largest dairy producer, Mengniu, is immediately ceasing work with Mbappe, saying it “firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people”.

The Shanghai Milkground ​Food Tech and Eastroc Beverage have followed suit, while drinks giant Dongpeng reportedly said the company “firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments.”

EFL Cup draw: Quarter-final lowdown including time, TV channel and stream

Draw details for the 2026/27 EFL Cup quarter-finals

Last Update:

The 2026/27 EFL Cup is about to go down to the final eight with the first quarter-finals in a major English competition of the season.

This season’s last-16 ties included a meeting between record 10-time champions Liverpool and Chelsea, who they beat in the 2023/24 final.

Manchester City will match the Reds’ record if they lift the trophy this season and Enzo Maresca’s side also faced an all-Premier League tie to reach the quarter-finals, facing Brighton & Hove Albion.

Here are all the details on how to watch the draw for the 2026/27 EFL Cup quarter-finals, including date, time, TV channel and live streams.

Carabao Cup: When is the draw for the EFL Cup quarter finals?

The draw will take place on Wednesday, October 28 after the tie between Andoni Iraola’s team and the Blues.

Presenter Dave Jones will host the draw alongside former England defenders Conor Coady and Graeme Le Saux.

What time is the EFL Cup quarter final draw?

The game at Anfield kicks off at 20:00 GMT (16:00 ET / 13:00 PT) and will go straight to penalties if the scoreline is level after 90 minutes.

That means the draw is likely to take place at approximately 22:00 GMT (18:00 ET / 15:00 PT), depending on added time and whether spot kicks are required.

EFL Cup: What channel is the Carabao Cup draw on?

All eight ties are on Sky Sports, with the game between Liverpool and Chelsea also available on ITV1.

Via Now TV, Sky Sports costs £14.99 for a day membership, £28 a month for a 12-month membership or £34.99 a month with no contract.

Carabao Cup draw stream online

Streaming is available on a vast variety of devices via the Sky GO app and the ITVX app.

EFL Cup fifth round draw ball numbers

The ball numbers will be published on the EFL website on Wednesday morning.

EFL Cup dates 2026/27: When are the Carabao Cup quarter-finals?

Here are the remaining dates in this season’s competition.

Do EFL Cup quarter final ties go to extra time, replays and penalties?

Should they finish level after 90 minutes, EFL Cup ties go straight to penalties until the semi-finals, which take place over two legs.

If the scoreline is level after the second leg, extra time and – if necessary – penalties are used to separate teams.

The final is a one-off match at Wembley Stadium, with extra time and penalties used if required.

EFL Cup quarter-final draw: Fixtures, schedule, TV channels

Here are the last-16 fixtures and how to watch. All times are GMT.

The EFL Cup winners receive a place in the play-off stage of the UEFA Conference League unless they qualify through another route for European competition.

Newcastle were an example of the rule in action in 2024/25, instead qualifying for the Champions League through their league position.

That meant their Conference League play-off place went to the next-highest ranked team who had not qualified for European competition via their league position.

articles.summary: Fleetwood recorded one of the great EFL Cup shocks
articles.content:
Fleetwood goalkeeper Lynch: We took inspiration from Grimsby beating Manchester United last year

Fleetwood recorded one of the great EFL Cup shocks

Last Update:

Fleetwood Town goalkeeper Jay Lynch said his side took inspiration from Grimsby beating Manchester United last year as they became the second League Two within the space of a year to knock a giant out of the Carabao Cup.

The Cod Army triumphed 5-3 on penalties to knock out Premier League champions Arsenal in the last 16 after a 1-1 draw in normal time for a victory which will go down as one of the greatest in League Cup history.

It was via penalties that fellow League Two side Grimsby dumped out Man Utd in the second round last year, but Fleetwood’s achievements may just top that after knocking out last year’s Premier League winners and Champions League finalists.

Keeper Lynch played a huge part, making a number of huge saves including one to deny Bruno Guimaraes in the shootout, and was ready to take in the jubilant scenes at HIghbury.

He told Sky Sports: “My voice has gone from organising the defence.

“The whole team throughout the game was magnificent. To beat the English champions – credit to these lads.

“We took heart from Grimsby beating Man Utd last year. We kind of compared it.

“A typical night in Fleetwood. We were expecting a storm, we knew the conditions would be horrible, so we thought it might go in our favour.

“Amazing for the club, the town. Honestly it means everything to everyone.”

Fleetwood boss Lawlor: The club’s greatest night

Fleetwood Town boss Matt Lawlor revelled in Fleetwood’s epic night, which he declared the best in the club’s history, having been a non-league side for much of their existence prior to 2012.

He said to Sky Sports: “It’s really hard to address the players. I’ve just said to enjoy it and then we’ve got a league game on Saturday and I didn’t want to be the bearer of the reality, but we’ve got a game. I just can’t believe it.

“The biggest night in the club’s history in terms of opposition coming to town and we’ve managed to beat the champions.

“We knew before the game, we’re not stupid enough and not egotistical enough that you think we’re going to go to the best team in the country and the most organised team in the country and the best of the basics and the world-class players, in that we’re going to go and outplay them.

“So we had to ride our luck, we had to deny space, we had to deny options for them. And I think we did that really, really well in terms of the majority of the game.

“Obviously, the goal happens, but they’re going to happen; they’re so good at football. The footballers that they have, the gaps that they find and we see it every week in the Premier League.

“I’m a big football fan and I watch the National League all the way through to the Premier League, Championship.

“So for me it was a tough game to prepare for, but I’m just so glad that the lads have the feeling the way they are and took that performance into make that town, the club, everyone proud.”

Kai Rooney can become a Man United professional in November

Kai Rooney scored four times inside 45 minutes as Manchester United won 6-0 at Burnley in the Under-18 Premier League on Tuesday.

Right-winger Rooney – son of United all-time top scorer Wayne – emulated his iconic father by sliding towards a corner flag on his knees, having fired in the 22nd-minute opener after Jaume Camacho headed against the woodwork at the Clarets’ training base.

Kai Rooney opens the scoring at Burnley for our #MUAcademy U18s 💪

Kai Rooney age: How old is Wayne Rooney’s eldest son?

Rooney turns 17 on Monday and has been at United since he was 11. His father joined the club for an initial £20 million from Everton in 2004.

Kai Rooney Manchester United scholarship

articles.title: Messi deserved Ballon d’Or and Kane’s triumph won’t ‘remove the stain’ of England’s World Cup semi-final defeat – Ole
articles.summary: Lionel Messi came fifth in the Ballon d'Or voting but one Argentinian newspaper says he deserved to win
articles.content:
Messi deserved Ballon d’Or and Kane’s triumph won’t ‘remove the stain’ of England’s World Cup semi-final defeat – Ole

Lionel Messi came fifth in the Ballon d'Or voting but one Argentinian newspaper says he deserved to win

Last Update:

Argentinian newspaper Ole claims Lionel Messi should have won the Ballon d’Or and insisted Harry Kane’s triumph “won’t remove the stain” of England’s World Cup semi-final defeat.

In an editorial, the newspaper suggested 2026 was a year in which the eight-time winner “most deserved” the award due to his exploits at the summer showpiece with Messi leading his country to the final where they lost to Spain.

Argentina beat England in a bad-tempered last-four clash after two late goals gave Lionel Scaloni’s side a 2-1 victory.

Messi, who did not travel to London for the ceremony – opting instead to attend the Messi Cup, an international youth tournament that carries his name – finished fifth in the voting, behind Kane, Kylian Mbappe, Lamine Yamal and Rodri.

He had returned to the shortlist for the first time in three years, at the age of 39, after also starring for Inter Miami, helping them win a maiden MLS Cup in December.

Ole commented: “Kane didn’t win the World Cup but achieved personal recognition. Among the merits of the 33-year-old striker we must recognise the incredible figure of 73 goals and 81 goal involvements [in 2026] between Bayern Munich and England.

“His performance at the World Cup also allowed him to leave Gary Lineker behind as England’s top scorer in the history of the tournament. With 14 goals to his name, he consolidated an outstanding trajectory that already had a highlight in Russia 2018, an edition in which he claimed the Golden Boot with six goals.

“Although the stain of having been defeated by Messi and Argentina, in the semi-finals in 2026, is one that will never be removed.”

‘The best will always be Leo Messi’

The article concluded: “With as many reasons as the other stars to have been chosen winner of this Ballon d’Or, the scoring record of a player with an exemplary profile was enough to give him the edge in one of the most even editions of recent times.

“But for us, the best is and always will be Leo Messi. The World Cup, once again, gave us evidence why.”

Messi recently retired from international football but continues to be a force in Major League Soccer.

He has a league-leading 25 goals this season but was left on the bench for the weekend defeat at the New York Red Bulls after making a trans-Atlantic dash back from Spain where he received the prestigious Princess of Asturias Award for Sports.

Messi is expected to return to the starting line-up when Miami face Cincinnati on Wednesday night.

articles.title: Michael Carrick dodges Manchester United sack AGAIN and will be in charge for Chelsea clash
articles.summary: Manchester United will give Michael Carrick another opportunity to prove he can be a success at Old Trafford
articles.content:
Michael Carrick dodges Manchester United sack AGAIN and will be in charge for Chelsea clash

Manchester United will give Michael Carrick another opportunity to prove he can be a success at Old Trafford

Last Update:

Michael Carrick will get another chance to steady the ship at Manchester United with the club having no plans to sack him before Saturday’s game at Chelsea.

United chiefs have spent two days assessing Carrick’s role at Old Trafford following the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth on Sunday but have opted against dismissing him and he will instead prepare the squad for the game at Stamford Bridge.

The news comes as something of a surprise given the game against Bournemouth was supposed to be Carrick’s final opportunity, coming just five days after a 4-1 humbling at Como in the Champions League.

United produced another lifeless performance against the Cherries, who could have won by a much larger margin than 3-0, a result that left Carrick’s side fifth bottom of the Premier League with just seven points from eight games.

The former England midfielder has presided over United’s worst top-flight start in 40 years and their worst of the Premier League era.

United will head to Chelsea on the back of an eight-game winless run in all competitions. They are not in EFL Cup action this week, having spurned a 2-0 lead to lose 3-2 at home to Brighton & Hove Albion in the third round.

Carrick has dilemma over United skipper Fernandes

Carrick was at the club’s Carrington training ground yesterday to watch United’s Under-21 side in a behind-closed-doors against Hull and took training as normal on Tuesday.

It was his first interaction with the first-team squad following Sunday’s game after which he appeared to say an emotional farewell to the United supporters, who sang his name before turning their ire on the players.

Carrick has a big decision to make regarding Bruno Fernandes’ involvement against Chelsea. The captain was left on the bench for the Bournemouth game after questioning the manager’s tactics in the defeat to Como.

He failed to make an appearance despite United’s struggles with Carrick instead bringing on the likes of Joshua Zirkzee and Shea Lacey.

It seems inconceivable the current PFA Player of the Year will start among the substitutes against Chelsea with Carrick’s job one again on the line.

If it does go wrong against Xabi Alonso’s men then United could be forced to make a change even though the contenders to succeed Carrick at Old Trafford look largely uninspiring.

The list is headed by Eddie Howe, who won one EFL Cup title at Newcastle despite a lavish spending spree under their Saudi Arabian owners, and also contains the likes of Antonio Conte and Julian Nagelsmann.

articles.content:
Why Kylian Mbappe and La Liga have said sorry to China

Kylian Mbappe came second in the Men's Ballon d'Or on Monday

Last Update:

Kylian Mbappe has apologised for hurting “many people in China and Chinese communities around the world”.

Real Madrid forward Mbappe said an “ill-judged” comment was “absolutely not my intention” following a reported backlash in the country over alleged remarks he made on YouTube show The Bridge, which is hosted by Blancos teammate Aurelien Tchouameni.

The top scorer in Spain last season issued a statement shortly after La Liga apologised to Chinese football fans on behalf of clubs, offered “respect” to China and said it is working on plans to build awareness of “different cultures”.

Chinese brands have dropped Mbappe over the reported remarks about “a Chinese dictator”, followed by a meme of his face being superimposed on an image resembling late Chinese leader Mao Zedong, according to the BBC.

Kylian Mbappe: Full apology to people in China

“During a recent interview, I reacted to an image featuring myself,” said Mbappe. “My comment was ill-judged and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world.

“I apologise to everyone my words have upset. That was absolutely not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history and I am sincerely sorry.”

What is Kylian Mbappe alleged to have said about China?

In unverified clips online, Mbappe does not name Mao but says he uses the meme “all the time” with friends, adding that it “makes me laugh the most… there’s a video of a guy, I think it’s a Chinese dictator…”

Chinese football forum Dongqiudi reportedly highlighted the interview, calling it “inappropriate” and liable to “hurt the feelings of Chinese people”.

Mao is an icon of the Communist Party in China, where the internet and digital content are subject to strict state control and the former leader is one of the most closely regulated topics.

Satire or jokes about the country’s founding leader from 1949 until his death in 1976 are ⁠considered disrespectful and a social taboo.

The original video is not on The Bridge’s YouTube channel and it is unclear when the episode first aired.

Mbappe spoke in September about memes depicting him as a dictator. “Part of it is funny because you get the sense that, for some people, it’s all in good fun,” he told L’Equipe.

“There’s also a less funny part because we know the damage these kinds of people have caused throughout history.

“To be compared to people who murder others, or who have made millions and millions of people unhappy… I don’t think I’ve ever done anything like that in my life.

“So there’s a mix of things. On the one hand, I know it’s done in a light-hearted way and doesn’t go that far, but it sometimes shows a lack of political and human awareness in people.”

Kylian Mbappe: Full La Liga statement

La Liga said it “deeply regrets the offence caused” to Chinese fans. “These comments were made in a personal capacity and do not represent La Liga,” it added.

“To the extent of our institutional responsibility, we apologize on behalf of La Liga and all its clubs.

“Spanish football upholds respect, coexistence, and unity among people of all cultures. We convey our respect to China, its institutions and its people and we deeply value the support of the millions of fans who follow us each week.

“We reaffirm our commitment to a relationship built over years. We are working with our partners and institutional interlocutors in China to address this situation.

“Likewise, in collaboration with the clubs and players, we will implement a protocol for awareness and communication that promotes respect for different cultures and helps prevent similar situations.”

Kylian Mbappe: What has the reaction been in China?

On Tuesday morning, four topics related to Mbappe remained among the top 10 trending searches on China’s social media platform, Weibo, Reuters reported.

The report said some internet critics had called ​for China to blacklist Mbappe ⁠and “reduce his commercial value to zero”, receiving hundreds of likes in response.

Reuters cited a spokesperson for China’s Foreign Ministry as saying that words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people “will naturally be met with joint opposition from all sectors of Chinese society.”

Confirmed Chinese brands to have dropped Mbappe

The country’s largest dairy producer, Mengniu, is immediately ceasing work with Mbappe, saying it “firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people”.

The Shanghai Milkground ​Food Tech and Eastroc Beverage have followed suit, while drinks giant Dongpeng reportedly said the company “firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments.”

The BBC cited a report by state-owned newspaper The Global Times that state broadcaster CCTV’s news apps will not feature Mbappe-related content and will stop showing La Liga matches.

articles.title: Carragher would have Real Madrid outcast Alexander-Arnold back at Liverpool…and give him plenty of stick!
articles.summary: Trent Alexander-Arnold left Liverpool under a cloud but the Reds' former centre-half Jamie Carragher would welcome him back to Anfield
articles.content:
Carragher would have Real Madrid outcast Alexander-Arnold back at Liverpool…and give him plenty of stick!

Trent Alexander-Arnold left Liverpool under a cloud but the Reds' former centre-half Jamie Carragher would welcome him back to Anfield

Last Update:

Jamie Carragher would love to see Trent Alexander-Arnold back at Liverpool.

Alexander-Arnold left Anfield for Real Madrid in controversial circumstances at the end of the 2024/25 season, the Spanish giants paying a reduced fee of around £10million after the full-back had run down his contract.

That undoubtedly tarnished the 28-year-old’s legacy on Merseyside, despite helping Liverpool to two Premier League titles, one Champions League crown, two EFL Cups and one FA Cup after coming through the club’s academy.

“I’d have him back,” said Carragher on the Overlap Fan Debate, brought to you by Sky Bet. “Give him plenty of stick… I think he made a mistake, I do. I think he made a big mistake. But, as I said, if something benefits Liverpool Football Club going forward… and we do have problems in terms of the right-back [position].

“Ronnie [Ronald Araujo] has been fantastic but we do have a problem in terms of full-backs passing. We’ve definitely missed his creativity.”

Trent is third-choice at Real Madrid – Carragher

Alexander-Arnold has failed to establish himself at Madrid, struggling for form and fitness under all three managers he has played for.

He started on the bench for Madrid’s Clasico win at Barcelona on Sunday, only appearing for the final few seconds as Jose Mourinho attempted to play down the clock.

Midfielder Federico Valverde started at right-back at Camp Nou and was replaced just after the hour mark by Denzel Dumfries.

Carragher added: “At the moment, he’s third choice right-back for Real Madrid. They’re playing a midfield player at right-back, and even in El Clásico, Denzel Dumfries, the first-choice right-back, if you like, comes on as a sub. So when you’re third choice at a club, they’re obviously wanting you to move on.”

Carragher believes Jacquet is first-choice at Liverpool

Should Alexander-Arnold return to Liverpool he would likely line up alongside Jeremy Jacquet, who has impressed next to Virgil van Dijk following his move from Rennes.

“I think he’s the first-choice centre-back and starting to look after Virgil a little bit rather than the other way around,” Carragher said of the France international. “And even though he’s only played eight games, I already feel he’s an upgrade on everybody else Virgil’s played alongside. I know it’s early to say that, but he really does look the part.

“And Virgil was always going to need that at some stage where he just has to play his own game. He can’t look after a back four. He can’t look after a centre-back partner. I think we’re at that stage now with Van Dijk, still playing well, but he should just be left to play his own game.”

‘Liverpool could be in a title race if they beat Arsenal’

Liverpool have lost just once in all competitions this season – 3-0 hammering at home to Manchester City – and sit fourth in the Premier League table following the weekend victory over Brighton.

They face Chelsea in the EFL Cup on Wednesday night before a big Premier League clash with champions Arsenal on Sunday.

Carragher said: “The thing I like right now is the fact that they’re getting results, things are going well, but I still think there’s a lot of improvement [to come]. When I watch the games, I still don’t think Liverpool have had one 90 minutes where you go, ‘everything was proper’. You know, three or four nil win, got the goals, looked solid at the back, kept the ball.

“I’ve never believed Liverpool are in a title race this season. But if you beat the champions and you’re closer in the table…

“We all look at [Andoni] Iraola’s squad and we probably say he’s been dealt a bad hand to a certain extent. What could Liverpool do in January that could propel them into a title race? If obviously the situation with [Manchester] City is resolved and they’re not actually in the title race, and you’re thinking it’s just Arsenal? It’s not actually the two teams we think we need to overtake, there’s just one now.”

articles.title: Bayern coach gives Vincent Kompany update: ‘He’s very calm’
articles.summary: Vincent Kompany has won the Bundesliga in each of his Bayern seasons
articles.content:
Bayern coach gives Vincent Kompany update: ‘He’s very calm’

Vincent Kompany has won the Bundesliga in each of his Bayern seasons

Last Update:

Bayern Munich assistant head coach Aaron Danks says manager Vincent Kompany is yet to receive a diagnosis after collapsing at the club’s training ground on Friday but is “in good spirits” in hospital and appears to be “getting better”.

Former Belgium and Manchester City defender Kompany missed Bayern’s 3-1 win at Freiburg in the Bundesliga on Sunday and received a “short visit” from Danks on Monday, the former Aston Villa coaching staff member said.

“He’s very calm,” said Danks, calling the improvement he perceived in Kompany’s condition “really positive”.

“It’s [about] letting him recover, rest and take his time, so nothing changes there. We had some good conversations but we kept it away from the football specifics, the tactics specifics.

“He asked how everything went, he asked how the players were. Apart from that, it was just a friendly chat. It was nice to see him and catch up.”

What happened to Vincent Kompany?

The 40-year-old had been suffering from a virus and missed Bayern’s press conference a day before their home game against Arsenal in the Champions League last Wednesday.

Kompany took charge for the 2-2 draw but collapsed while watching Bayern’s reserve team two days later.

“The fact is, we protect our coach wherever we can,” Roten director of sport Max Eberl said after Kompany was admitted.

“If a coach says he feels ready to do something, then we’re not going to say ‘we won’t allow that’ if we don’t know what’s going on.

“It’s also everyone’s own responsibility to say ‘I can’t carry on now’.”

How long has Vincent Kompany been in hospital for?

Kompany had been in hospital for four days when Danks spoke on October 27, a day before Bayern were scheduled to host second-tier Magdeburg in the second round of the German Cup.

When could Vincent Kompany return after collapse?

“There are no major updates in terms of diagnosis or return to work – nothing like that at the moment,” said Danks.

Eberl emphasised that everyone at the club should be “clear” on expecting Kompany to return in weeks rather than days.

“Vinnie will be given all the time he needs,” added Eberl. “We’re not starting to put together any timeframes.

“We need to firstly figure out what it is. Then we’ll discuss calmly what the recovery time is to be.”

Ballon d’Or 2026: Harry Kane triumph makes Aaron Danks ‘proud’

Danks admitted that he had not necessarily expected Bayern talisman Harry Kane to win the Ballon d’Or on Monday.

“I can’t say I was overly confident – he had to hold his own against top players,” explained Danks. “The margins were very tight.

“We work very closely with him and see the effort he puts in. As an Englishman, I’m not entirely impartial here, but I see how hard he works every day.

“I’m delighted for him and also for the club; it shows what the club stands for. I’m very proud. I’m also very pleased that Harry has won this for England, as the first player to do so since Michael Owen [in 2001].

“He’ll now come back and carry on in his usual professional and humble way.”

Some observers have speculated that Kane’s remarks about being willing to “work hard in silence” and “let success be your noise” may have been directed at the likes of rival Lamine Yamal.

“Harry’s statement was fantastic for all young players; he wasn’t addressing it to anyone in particular,” said Danks.

“He works incredibly hard to be well prepared. His success speaks for itself. A few years ago, many people said he’d never win anything.

“Those things are coming his way now; he’s letting his success speak for itself.”

Bayern Munich fixtures, schedule

Kane could feature when holders Bayern play their German Cup tie. “It’s a fantastic moment for him and a great achievement,” said Danks.

“He’ll be reporting back with the other players that travelled. They’re due back at lunchtime [on Tuesday], so he’ll practice this afternoon and be available.”

Bayern then face Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga in Der Klassiker on Saturday.
