articles.title: Why me? Kvaratskhelia posts emotional message after ACL blow that will sideline PSG star for rest of the season
articles.summary: PSG winger Kvaratskhelia believes his injury will help protect other players
articles.content:
Why me? Kvaratskhelia posts emotional message after ACL blow that will sideline PSG star for rest of the season

PSG winger Kvaratskhelia believes his injury will help protect other players

Last Update:

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia has vowed to come back stronger after sustaining a ruptured ACL and claimed he was chosen by God to help protect other players from injury.

The Paris Saint-Germain winger sustained the setback last night during the 4-2 Champions League win over Barcelona at the Parc des Princes, falling awkwardly after challenging Xavi Espart.

He will undergo an operation in the coming days and won’t play again this season.

It is a crushing blow for the 25-year-old and for PSG, who will now go in search of a third successive Champions League success without the brilliant Georgian.

Kvaratskhelia wrote on social media: “Why me? I was not ready for this.

“Many people have asked me questions about this setback, many have said that if all the footballers in the world prayed, the match would end in a draw. That might be true, but before every match I play, I ask God to leave the field unscathed, but in vain.

“It hasn’t been long, but it’s still in my head – why me? I’ve never missed anything, probably prepared for this game the best I’ve ever prepared. I thought I was prepared for everything, but no. I realise that God has chosen me and if I was protecting the players on another field, I’m ready to go through these months of work, pain, tears.

“I know I have to come back stronger for my people who always support me, I won’t let you down, I promise I won’t waste a second. Thank you all for your support, see you soon.”

Kvaratskhelia one of three injury blows for PSG

There was early concern when Kvaratskhelia was helped off just short of the hour mark last night and PSG’s worst fears were confirmed this morning following tests.

A PSG medical update read: “Victim of a rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament of the right knee during yesterday’s match against FC Barcelona, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia will undergo surgery in the coming days.”

The medical update also revealed both Ousmane Dembele and captain Marquinhos sustained thigh injuries that will keep them out for several weeks.

Speaking after the game, PSG boss Luis Enrique admitted his frustration at the prospect of having to do without three key players at an important stage of the season.

“I am not the doctor. I am the coach,” he said. “The three injuries is the worst part of the game today. We will have to wait for the tests tomorrow. They are three very important players, so it’s really bad news, of course, but that’s football.”

It is the loss of Kvaratskhelia that will hurt the Parisians most, though.

The supremely gifted playmaker, nicknamed ‘Kvaradona’ by fans of former club Napoli in homage to the great Diego Maradona, is a major part of PSG’s attacking arsenal.

He has scored 29 goals in 91 games for PSG in all competitions.

articles.content:
Bayern Munich midfielder Kimmich to miss Arsenal game due to family bereavement

Bayern Munich will be without one of their most influential players against Arsenal in the Champions League tonight

Last Update:

Joshua Kimmich will miss Wednesday night’s Champions League game with Arsenal due to a family bereavement, Bayern Munich announced this morning.

The Bayern captain was absent from training yesterday and won’t be considered for the fixture with the Gunners at the Allianz Arena.

A club statement read: “Due to a passing in his immediate family, Joshua Kimmich is not in the squad today for the match against Arsenal.

“On behalf of the family, we ask that his privacy and grief be respected, and that further inquiries and reporting be refrained from.

“We send our deepest condolences to Joshua Kimmich and his loved ones.”

In Kimmich’s absence, Aleksandar Pavlovic and Tom Bischof could form the central midfield pairing for the Bundesliga leaders.

Bayern boss Kompany struggling to be fit for Arsenal clash

Kimmich’s absence continues a disrupted build-up to the game for Bayern, who are without star midfielder Michael Olise through suspension following his red card against Viking in their last Champions League outing.

Coach Vincent Kompany missed Tuesday’s media conference as he battles to shrug off a virus with his assistant Aaron Danks speaking to the press.

Danks said: ”Vincent has a virus. It’s important that he rests. He’s at home resting. We take it day by day. We’re in constant communication. He’ll play his role and part in the game – whether that’s at the Allianz Arena or not, we’ll have to wait and see.

“It has affected his legs at times, he found some pain in his legs. It’s just a virus. The doctors know way more than I do. The most important thing is that he rests and takes the time he needs. I don’t know whether that will be tomorrow or 2-3 days. We’re taking it day by day.

“For me, not much changes. I plan the training sessions every day. Obviously we miss Vincent, but we have a strong coaching team, we know what needs to be done. We need to stay calm and keep the players’ energy high so they are ready tomorrow.”

Andoni Iraola warns Liverpool players ‘cannot relax’ despite fighting back in Champions League win

Andoni Iraola has opened up on a tough night in the Champions League for Liverpool

Last Update:

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has warned his players they cannot afford to switch off against top opposition after coming from behind to beat Villarreal in the Champions League.

The Reds recovered from a difficult first half to secure the win at Anfield, but Iraola was frustrated by his side’s defensive mistakes and admitted they have been conceding too many goals this season.

Speaking to Amazon Prime after the match, the Liverpool boss praised his team’s response while insisting there is still plenty to improve.

“A lot of things happened today. They were much better than us in the first half and we were much better in the second half,” Iraola said.

“When we’ve been under pressure, we answered well. When we relaxed, we made mistakes. You cannot relax against very good opposition. I value the win.

“We have to know that if we don’t go to the limit, it will be difficult. We are facing very good teams. It’s good to come back but we’ve started losing too many goals this season.”

Iraola praises Rio Ngumoha’s development

One positive for Liverpool was the performance of 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha, who continues to earn opportunities under Iraola and registered two assists on Tuesday night.

The manager believes the youngster is becoming a more rounded player, particularly after adapting to a role on the right flank.

“I am really happy wth Rio. He is trying to improve everything that we try to correct,” Iraola said.

“He is playing a lot more on the right and he has adapted really well. He’s going more inside. He struggled defensively in the first half, second half was much better. He’s becoming a more complete oayer. He’s still only 18.”

Champions League: Alvarez off the mark as Atletico held, Napoli claim thrilling win

Atletico were able to hold on for a point despite a second-half red card.

Last Update:

Champions League headlines

Holders PSG end Barcelona winning run in Parc des Princes thriller

Wirtz on target as Liverpool fight back to beat Villarreal

Man City cruise past AEK

Alvarez earns point for Atletico

Julian Alvarez scored his first goal of the season for 10-man Atletico Madrid as they came from behind to draw 1-1 with Stuttgart in the Champions League.

Stuttgart looked on course for three wins from three to start the league phase when Jamie Leweling drilled home a low effort to break the deadlock in the 36th minute.

However, Alvarez, who failed in his bid to force through a move to Barcelona in the summer, responded two minutes into the second half, finding the top-right corner with a first-time finish from Ademola Lookman’s pass.

Atletico were reduced to 10 in the 64th minute when Morten Hjulmand saw red for an awful challenge on Angelo Stiller. However, Stuttgart could not make their extra man count.

Their Bundesliga rivals Borussia Dortmund bounced back from defeat to Bodo/Glimt last time out as a Serhou Guirassy double gave them a 2-1 win over Sabah in Azerbaijan.

Bodo, meanwhile, made Napoli work extremely hard for their first win of the league phase.

Matteo Politano opened the scoring in Naples after just 53 seconds, only for Bodo to restore parity when Jens Petter Hauge slotted into the bottom-right corner.

Scott McTominay put Napoli in front again in the 41st minute, only for Andreas Helmersen to equalise as Bodo responded once again.

Yet McTominay doubled his tally with a close-range header to give Napoli the lead for a third time, and an own goal from Odin Bjortuft made the points safe for the hosts before Sondre Brunstad Fet pulled one back in stoppage time.

Roma joined Napoli in claiming a first victory of the league phase, thumping Slovan Bratislava 4-0, but it is three defeats from three for Portuguese champions Porto after Guus Til’s effort gave PSV Eindhoven victory at Estadio do Dragao.

Elsewhere, Slavia Prague earned their first point of the phase as Pavel Kacor’s injury-time goal earned them a 2-2 draw at Fenerbahce.

Cesc Fabregas hits back at ‘not very nice’ Manchester United job question as Michael Carrick faces growing pressure

Cesc Fabregas has been asked about taking over from Manchester United boss Michael Carrick.

Last Update:

Como manager Cesc Fabregas has dismissed speculation linking him with the Manchester United job, insisting it is disrespectful to discuss replacing Michael Carrick while he remains in charge.

Fabregas will come up against Carrick on Wednesday evening when Como host United in the Champions League, with the visitors desperate to end a six-match winless run.

The former Arsenal, Chelsea and Barcelona midfielder was asked during his pre-match press conference whether he would consider taking over at Old Trafford.

However, he refused to entertain the suggestion and instead defended his opposite number.

“I won’t answer that question because I think that’s not a very nice question,” Fabregas said on Tuesday.

“I don’t think that shows enough respect to a great footballer and manager like Michael Carrick at the helm of a wonderful Manchester United side.

“Manchester United is a historical club I know very, very well,” he continued.

“We have so much respect for who they are, for what they do, because they have incredible players.

“I know Steve Holland very well because I worked with him for years at Chelsea and I know Michael has done really well in previous clubs as well.

“Last year he did really well bringing Manchester United back to where they belong, which is the Champions League, for the first time in many years, so it’s not all bad. It’s an honour to host them for the first time in our history.”

While United arrive in Italy struggling for form, Como have enjoyed an encouraging start to their domestic campaign.

Fabregas’ side sit fifth in Serie A and head into Wednesday’s European encounter following a 3-1 win over Fiorentina on Sunday.

articles.content:
Jose Mourinho sends Vinicius Junior warning: ‘Only the badge is untouchable’

Jose Mourinho has warned Vinicius Junior that his place at Real Madrid is never safe.

Last Update:

Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has warned Vinicius Junior that no player is guaranteed a place in his starting XI ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League clash with RB Leipzig.

The Brazilian has endured a difficult start to the season, scoring just once in all competitions, and faces increasing competition for his place from summer signing Yan Diomande.

Vinicius is currently serving a four-match suspension in LaLiga but remains available in Europe, where he struggled during last week’s dramatic 4-3 win over Roma.

He was substituted after 58 minutes, with replacement Endrick helping inspire Madrid’s comeback.

Speaking at his pre-match press conference, Mourinho made clear that reputation and previous achievements would not guarantee anyone a place in his team.

“Only the badge is untouchable,” Mourinho said.

“I don’t like the concept of ‘untouchable’ players. What makes players untouchable isn’t a captain’s armband, or how long they’ve been at the club, or their status. What makes a player untouchable is performance.”

Mourinho has always supported Vinicius despite his struggles, but recent performances from other attacking players have given the Portuguese manager additional options.

“As I said recently, I’m not a stubborn coach,” he explained.

“There are coaches who have an idea, and live or die by that idea. I’m not that kind of coach, I’m always open to analyse, to understand things and look for the best for the team.”

Mourinho plays down Real Madrid’s Champions League ambitions

Madrid have won their opening two Champions League matches against Inter Milan and Roma, but Mourinho refused to describe his side as contenders for the trophy.

“It’s very early,” he said.

“Right now Real Madrid don’t have the objective of winning the Champions League. We have the objective of qualifying [for the knockout phase].

“Then, if we get the points that allow us to qualify, then we get to our second objective, to try to avoid the playoffs, which are two games with tension, and they’re games you can avoid.”

Madrid also face a big challenge in LaLiga, sitting six points behind Barcelona ahead of Sunday’s Clasico at Camp Nou.

articles.title: Ex-Arsenal winger Gnabry eager to shine for Bayern Munich against former mentor Arteta
articles.summary: Bayern Munich host Arsenal in the Champions League on Wednesday night and there will be an emotional reunion between Gunners boss Mikel Arteta and his former team-mate Serge Gnabry...
articles.content:
Ex-Arsenal winger Gnabry eager to shine for Bayern Munich against former mentor Arteta

Bayern Munich host Arsenal in the Champions League on Wednesday night and there will be an emotional reunion between Gunners boss Mikel Arteta and his former team-mate Serge Gnabry...

Last Update:

Serge Gnabry revealed his admiration for “leader” Mikel Arteta but intends to bring down the Arsenal boss on Wednesday night.

Gnabry played alongside Arteta when they were team-mates with the Gunners but the pair will come face to face at the Allianz Arena when the Germany winger lines up for Bayern Munich in their Champions League clash.

The 31-year-old is now an experienced player having made over 200 appearances for Bayern and won 62 international caps but he has not forgotten the impact Arteta had on him earlier in his career.

“He was a leader in the team back then, also our captain,” he said. “He talked a lot with young players like me and Hector Bellerin and always had an open ear for us. That shows what kind of personality he has. He led the team to this great success last season [when Arsenal won the Premier League title]. He’s doing a very good job.”

It’s a special game against Arsenal – Bayern star Gnabry

That does not mean Gnabry, who is likely to return to the squad from injury tomorrow with Michael Olise suspended, will be holding back against his former mentor.

He added: ”It’s always a special game against a former club. I grew up there and I’m really looking forward to it. It’s a bit strange to play against a coach you used to play with. We want to win, that’s what it’s all about. I’m looking forward to the game.

“A game against Arsenal, given my history, is always special. I’m happy to be back after a long injury layoff. I’m grateful for every minute I get. I need the game time to get back into shape. I’m happy when I play, but the most important thing is that we win as a team.”

Arteta could miss out on another reunion tomorrow, though, with Bayern boss Vincent Kompany, who worked with the Spaniard at Manchester City, struggling with a virus.

One of his assistants Aaron Danks took Tuesday’s pre-match press conference and admitted he did not know if the Belgian would be able to take his place in the dugout.

Danks said: ”Vincent has a virus. It’s important that he rests. He’s at home resting. We take it day by day. We’re in constant communication. He’ll play his role and part in the game – whether that’s at the Allianz Arena or not, we’ll have to wait and see.

“It has affected his legs at times, he found some pain in his legs. It’s just a virus. The doctors know way more than I do. The most important thing is that he rests and takes the time he needs. I don’t know whether that will be tomorrow or 2-3 days. We’re taking it day by day.

“For me, not much changes. I plan the training sessions every day. Obviously we miss Vincent, but we have a strong coaching team, we know what needs to be done. We need to stay calm and keep the players’ energy high so they are ready tomorrow.”

Bayern assistant coach Danks coy on Neuer involvement against Arsenal

Midfielder Joshua Kimmich missed today’s training session to attend a personal matter while veteran goalkeeper Manuel Neuer will be given more time to prove his fitness from a foot injury.

“We haven’t made a decision yet,” said Danks. “Manu has been back on the grass for two days, which is fantastic. We’ll meet as a coaching team, speak to Vince and speak to the goalkeeping coach. At the moment there’s no decision made, but it’s great that Manu is back.”

One man who will be desperate to get one over on Arsenal is former Tottenham striker Harry Kane.

The England captain has been in blistering form in recent weeks and is one of the leading contenders to win the Ballon d’Or in London on Monday night.

“I’m really biased when it comes to Harry because I’m an Englishman,” admitted Danks. “It’s a privilege to work with Harry and see his level every day. His overall game is at such a high level that could also be our best defender and our best playmaker in training, he can score goals. I learn a lot from working with him. The level here at Bayern Munich is very high.”

articles.title: Real Madrid TV rubbish Guler elbow theory and claim Barcelona will have 17 referees in El Clasico
articles.summary: There is no sign of the tedious squabbling between Real Madrid and Barcelona calming ahead of Sunday's Clasico at Camp Nou
articles.content:
Real Madrid TV rubbish Guler elbow theory and claim Barcelona will have 17 referees in El Clasico

There is no sign of the tedious squabbling between Real Madrid and Barcelona calming ahead of Sunday's Clasico at Camp Nou

Last Update:

Real Madrid TV, the unofficial mouthpiece of the club, claim there will be 17 referees against Jose Mourinho’s men when they face Barcelona in El Clasico on Sunday.

The sides meet at Camp Nou after another hugely controversial weekend in La Liga with both clubs accused of benefitting from favourable refereeing decisions.

Madrid beat Sevilla 4-1 but were fortunate referee Mateo Busquets Ferrer did not see a first-half incident in which midfielder Arda Guler elbowed the visitors’ Peque Fernandez in the face.

Guler went on to score the opener with Sevilla boss Luis Garcia Plaza claiming afterwards the officials opted not to intervene to enable Madrid to keep within touching distance of leaders Barca ahead of their eagerly anticipated meeting.

Barcelona influenced the referee, say Real Madrid TV

Barca were also caught in a storm 24 hours earlier, during their 5-2 win at Real Betis. The home side had a goal ruled out after Cucho Hernandez was deemed to have handled the ball before Giovani Lo Celso smashed home a brilliant volley.

Referee Ricardo de Burgos was initially unaware of Hernandez’s misdemeanour but the clamour from the Barca players – led by Pedri and Lamine Yamal – persuaded him to have a conversation with the VAR and the goal was overturned.

That has prompted RMTV to claim the on-field official was influenced by the Barca players.

They claimed on Tuesday: “Real Madrid will have to face 17 referees in the Clasico: the three on the field, the fourth referee, the VAR and his assistant, in addition to the eleven players of Barcelona, who are also referees. Against 17 referees it is very complicated.

“The Barça players now decide which plays are reviewed by the VAR and which are not, because they are also referees. It’s outrageous. In any other league it would have consequences. Sunday is very complicated because of the issues we all know.”

Real Madrid TV brush off accusations of Guler elbow

Unsurprisingly, RMTV had a different take on the Guler case than most neutral observers and dismissed theories that there weren’t enough camera shots taken of the incident which occurred well away from the ball.

They added: “[We are] against everything and against everyone. Against a regime and a media system in which there are synchronized opinions that only talk about an inconclusive play of Güler and Peque, when the player was also being repeatedly grabbed.

“Now they say that images are missing, when on RMTV we have been denouncing for years that there are shots that are not shown in the broadcasts and they called us conspiratorial. An inconclusive play is enough for everything to change.”

Both teams face Champions League games before they lock horns at the weekend.

Barca face two-time defending champions Paris Saint-Germain at the Parc des Princes on Tuesday before Madrid host RB Leipzig 24 hours later.

articles.title: Champions League predictions: Full guide to Matchday 3 2026/27
articles.summary: The lowdown on Champions League Matchday 3
articles.content:
Champions League predictions: Full guide to Matchday 3 2026/27

The lowdown on Champions League Matchday 3

Last Update:

Europe’s elite face a tough task to match the record-breakingly extravagant entertainment of Champions League Matchday 2.

With the ball hitting the net 78 times, the fixture list produced the most-ever Champions League goals in a single week, including Liverpool’s 6-3 win at LASK, Brugge’s 4-3 victory at Inter and Viking’s surprise 3-3 draw at home to Bayern Munich, the Norwegian side opening the scoring after two minutes and netting the decisive goal in the 90th.

Fortunately, there is a precedent for a blockbuster Matchday 3: the previous record was set across the third round of league phase games last season, which also featured 18 matches and delivered 71 goals, even allowing for a 0-0 draw involving Tottenham.

PSG hit seven, Barcelona bagged six and Liverpool netted five on that occasion. Goals galore again? Let’s take a look at a selection of key fixtures.

Champions League fixtures this week: PSG vs Barcelona

The defending double champions meet five-time winners Barca again, having beaten the dominant force in La Liga 2-1 away in last season’s league phase.

Ferran Torres scored the opener for the Spanish side on that occasion and the new PSG signing is at the centre of a succession of intriguing subplots in this game, including Paris coach Luis Enrique’s emotional ties to opponents with whom he won the competition as part of a treble in 2014/15.

Both teams have six points and forwards in formidable form: PSG’s Ousmane Dembele has three goals and three assists in this season’s Champions League, while Barca’s Lamine Yamal has set up four goals and scored once, including two assists in a 4-1 win at Galatasaray on Tuesday.

PSG’s 4-2 win at Manchester City the following day was even more impressive, including three goals without reply by Desire Doue, Dembele and Vitinha inside the first 33 minutes to help the Ligue 1 title holders end the Premier League leaders’ perfect start in all competitions.

Prediction: PSG 2-2 Barcelona

Man City vs AEK Athens: Visitors seek Champions League history

Antoine Semenyo said City had misapplied their press during the first half against PSG and Enzo Maresca’s side were much-improved after the break, netting twice through joint-competition top scorer Erling Haaland to take the in-form striker’s total to four in the league phase.

Haaland broke Lionel Messi’s record as the fastest player to 60 Champions League goals and has averaged more than a goal a game in the competition during his career – cause for concern for Athens fans after their side’s unblemished three-match defensive record since the start of qualifying came to an end with a 3-1 defeat at Shakhtar on Wednesday.

AEK hit the woodwork three times at Stamford Bridge and are unbeaten in the Greek Super League but have never won away in the Champions League proper and possess a wretched record against English sides in the competition, losing seven times and winning once.

As well as rewarding brave bets, the huge underdogs will become the first Greek team ever to beat City if they spring a surprise, with the English club yet to concede in four such games, winning three of them.

Prediction: Man City 3-0 AEK Athens

Stuttgart vs Atletico Madrid: Seven in a row for La Liga giants?

Stuttgart followed up a 3-1 home win over Viking with a 3-0 victory at Slovan Bratislava on Wednesday but their uncertain start to their domestic season continued with a fourth defeat in their opening six league games on Saturday, losing to an 88th-minute goal at Hamburg.

Stats experts gave Miro Muheim’s winning strike a 3% probability from the position he shot from and the xG numbers also made painful reading for a Stuttgart side who finished on 2.67 to their opponents’ 0.93.

A first win against a Spanish team at the eighth attempt in the competition would be the perfect tonic for Stuttgart, and Atleti’s record of five defeats in their six trips to Germany might provide encouragement.

Atleti’s only victory in Germany came almost exactly 30 years ago at Dortmund, but their form bodes well for changing that on forward Ademola Lookman’s 29th birthday.

Second in Spain, dominant Atleti beat Espanyol through Alex Baena’s 89th-minute goal on Saturday to extend their winning run to six matches in all competitions, including their first points of the league phase last Tuesday with a 2-0 home win over Manchester United.

Prediction: Stuttgart 0-0 Atletico Madrid

Liverpool vs Villarreal: Isak, Barcola, Wirtz finding form

Yet to show their best in the Premier League, Liverpool have given Andoni Iraola a memorable start to managing in the Champions League with a home win over Atleti and a 6-3 victory at LASK on Wednesday in which they were 4-0 ahead after 51 minutes.

New £123 million signing Bradley Barcola scored a hat-trick in Linz and the Reds’ expensively-assembled attack helped them to another win at Brentford on Saturday, capitalising after their opponents were reduced to ten players with a winner from Alexander Isak and assists for Barcola and Florian Wirtz.

Twelfth in Spain, Villarreal have never beaten an English team in 16 attempts in the Champions League but ended a 12-game winless run in the competition by coming from behind to beat Napoli 3-1 at home last Tuesday.

There were five goals when these teams met in the second leg of the 2021/22 semi-finals, the Yellow Submarine scoring twice inside the first 42 minutes at home to level the tie before Fabinho, Luis Diaz and Sadio Mane’s second-half goals gave Liverpool a 5-2 aggregate win.

Prediction: Liverpool 1-0 Villarreal

Champions League Matchday 3: Real Madrid vs Leipzig

Having scored in successive Liga games with the final goal in Madrid’s 4-1 home win over Sevilla on Sunday, Yan Diomande will be reunited with the team who sold the Ivory Coast winger in August for a fee that could rise to £120m.

Diomande and Madrid will want a less dramatic night than Los Blancos had at Roma on Wednesday, falling behind twice and trailing 3-1 in the 82nd minute of their 4-3 win to stay perfect following their home victory over Inter on Matchday 1.

Madrid have won all of their six home matches in all competitions this season, which is ominous for a Leipzig side who have lost all four of their away matches in the 2026/27 Bundesliga and Champions League, including a 6-1 hammering at Bayern on Saturday.

Head coach Martin Demichelis apologised afterwards to Leipzig’s supporters, who also saw their team lose 4-1 at Como on Matchday 1 to extend their losing run in group stage and league phase games to six matches.

Prediction: Real Madrid 4-1 Leipzig

Como vs Manchester United: Premier League strugglers on road

Cesc Fabregas’ Como won for the first time in four matches in all competitions with a 3-1 victory at Fiorentina on Sunday and the Champions League newcomers may feel the visit of Manchester United is a particularly presentable chance to recover from their 3-2 defeat at Feyenoord on Matchday 2.

Winger Assane Diao scored the opener against the Dutch side, while Tasos Douvikas’ late consolation means that the duo have scored in each of the club’s league phase games, following up a 4-1 home win over Leipzig.

Back in the misty days of Michael Carrick’s first spell as United caretaker, the former Red Devils midfielder oversaw their only win in their last 10 Champions League away matches with a 2-0 victory at Villarreal in November 2021.

United have lost six times across that poor run on the road and their performance in a 1-1 draw at Leeds United on Sunday – increasing the malaise around Carrick and leaving them with one win from their first seven league games – gave little indication that their form is about to improve.

Prediction: Como 3-1 Manchester United

Bayern Munich vs Arsenal: Harry Kane chases perfect 10

Invincible runs meet unstoppable forces when the reigning German and English champions meet in a mightily unpredictable-looking early-season clash of contenders in Munich.

Viking showed that Bayern can be troubled but Harry Kane scored twice for Vincent Kompany’s team and the Tottenham all-time top scorer now has the chance to register in a 10th straight Champions League outing and enhance a record of 15 goals in 22 appearances against Arsenal.

The Gunners were functional rather than flowing in beating Nottingham Forest away on Sunday but have won their last 14 league phase matches, although they have five defeats and one victory in their eight most recent visits to Germany.

A hard-earned 3-0 home win over Lille was on par for Arsenal on Matchday 2 and their achievement will be far more special if they end Bayern’s 39-match unbeaten home run in league phase and group stage games, dropping points twice along the way.

Prediction: Bayern Munich 3-2 Arsenal

Aston Villa vs Viking: Premier League club target 12 in a row

After a slow start in the Premier League, Aston Villa and an injury-free Johan Manzambi are starting to purr and the £51.1m signing took his tally to three goals in his last four appearances by netting in the 6-0 home win over Fenerbahce on Wednesday and 1-0 victory at Newcastle on Saturday.

Villa are the only team who can match PSG and Barca’s six points and plus-seven goal difference in this season’s league phase, although Viking – making their debut in the competition proper – proved they can upset the odds with that draw against Bayern.

Captain Zlatko Tripic has a goal and two assists in this season’s Champions League and Viking have previous with English sides, knocking Chelsea out of the 2002/03 UEFA Cup.

Viking’s defeat at Stuttgart and Villa’s imperious continental form suggest the Dark Blues will need to step up their performance again, aiming to end two of their opponents’ dazzling club-record runs.

The Villans are on a 14-match unbeaten European home stretch and have won their last 11 such games at Villa Park. As Fener can testify, Villa can be hard to halt.

Prediction: Aston Villa 2-0 Viking

Here’s the full list of fixtures on Matchday 3, as well as UK broadcaster details.

Amazon have first pick of the Tuesday games, with all the other matches shown on TNT Sports. BBC Sport also has highlights rights.

Matches on TNT Sports can be streamed through the HBO Max app. Subscriptions start at £30.99 a month including Eurosport and entertainment and are available on a vast range of devices including smart TVs and gaming consoles.

articles.title: ‘He didn’t prepare himself’ – Ten Hag says lazy Ronaldo was not fit during second stint at Manchester United
articles.summary: Erik ten Hag says Cristiano Ronaldo 'did not run in possession or out of possession' at Manchester United because he was not fit
articles.content:
‘He didn’t prepare himself’ – Ten Hag says lazy Ronaldo was not fit during second stint at Manchester United

Erik ten Hag says Cristiano Ronaldo 'did not run in possession or out of possession' at Manchester United because he was not fit

Last Update:

Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag claims Cristiano Ronaldo flopped during his second spell at Old Trafford because he did not work hard enough in training.

In a wide-ranging interview with The Athletic, Ten Hag says the Portugal international “did not prepare himself” for the rigours of Premier League football and failed to get himself in top shape.

Ten Hag, who is now technical director of his boyhood team FC Twente, also claims he pushed to sign Frenkie de Jong, Declan Rice and Harry Kane during his time at United only to be let down on each occasion.

Ronaldo rejoined United in August 2021 and Ten Hag met him following his appointment as boss at the end of the 2021/22 season.

“He let the team down, and he let me down, because we planned with him,” says Ten Hag. “I flew out to Portugal to speak with him about what I was aiming for before I came to United. Obviously, he’s one of the best in football history. I respected him a lot. But at that time, as a manager, I had to make a rational decision and keep the players I admire in.”

Ronaldo did not work for the team at Man United – Ten Hag

The situation eventually came to a head with Ronaldo, by then a regular substitute, demanding to leave the club before his contract was terminated in November 2022. He subsequently joined Saudi Arabian side Al-Nassr.

“Many times I say, ‘Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can’t bring yourself in the box, you can’t score’. He was not capable to do this. It’s the wrong idea to put this to me that I expected him to do the pressing, that he’s exhausted. But he couldn’t. He ran neither in possession nor out of possession. The reason was because he didn’t prepare himself.

“Every top team has to embrace the top player, but the top player has to work for the team.

“He was telling the players, ‘Save your legs at the training’. I understand it when you are top fit; you have sessions, you can save the legs. But first you have to train yourself to get into the right fitness levels.”

Ten Hag made his name as an elite coach after guiding Ajax to the Champions League semi-finals in 2019 with a stylish young side.

After being recruited by former United chief executive Richard Arnold and football director John Murtough he outlined his vision to guide the club back to the top of the English game.

De Jong, Rice and Kane all failed to join United

His ambitious targets included Barcelona star De Jong.

“Everyone’s thinking the manager is doing the negotiations, that I’m involved in financial issues, but I was never,” says Ten Hag. “Of course, I did my best; I set up meetings with him, where it was Richard and John involved as well, to pursuade him to come over. He could have been very important building the team, not only that year but for the future. But we didn’t make it.”

Second choice was Rice, then at West Ham, who has gone on to become one of the best central midfielders in the Premier League and played a pivotal role in Arsenal’s title success last season.

Ten Hag added: “The issue was that West Ham didn’t want to let him go. I think we could have done more to test. We were on one page, they tried, but I don’t know how the process went. The point is, at United you need outstanding players.”

In attack, Ten Hag was desperate to bring in Kane, who instead joined Bayern Munich from Tottenham and has scored 157 goals in 155 games for the Bundesliga champions.

“I fought for it. I heard that he was very positive, but I never spoke with him about the issue,” he said. “I don’t know how the decision process went with John, Richard, the Glazers.”

articles.title: De Zerbi hails Tottenham as ‘very good team’ after Spurs end winless run
articles.summary: De Zerbi hailed the spirit of his side after they ended their winless run.
articles.content:
De Zerbi hails Tottenham as ‘very good team’ after Spurs end winless run

De Zerbi hailed the spirit of his side after they ended their winless run.

Last Update:

A delighted Roberto De Zerbi praised Tottenham as “a very good team” after they claimed their first Premier League win of the season by beating Coventry City 3-1.

Spurs had begun the season without a win in six in the league, but James Maddison’s goal on his first start since May last year put them on course for victory.

Jack Rudoni equalised four minutes into the second half. However, Omar Marmoush’s first Tottenham goal and a stoppage-time strike from Ben Davies clinched a win that moved Tottenham out of the relegation zone.

De Zerbi has previously been publicly critical of his side amid their struggles, pointing to problems with mentality.

However, he was full of plaudits for his players following their long-awaited triumph.

“I am delighted for the result, the attitude, the spirit and the reaction after the goal we conceded,” De Zerbi told Sky Sports.

“Honestly we did not play so well like the last games. But now for our responsibility they deserve credit as they defended very well and compact.

“Now we have to understand we are able to win because after two or three seasons like this the mental aspect is crucial.

“We have to thank the fans, especially in the last part of the game they were fantastic, They have suffered a lot.

“We have to push, we have to improve the quality of the play for sure but we are a good team, a very good team.”

Coventry failed to claim a third successive win, but manager Frank Lampard still saw reasons for positives.

“The first half I thought we were really good. Hard to say after a 3-1 defeat,” Lampard said to Sky Sports.

“I think the last goal was obviously a mistake. I think it distorts the picture of the game.

“I think the players showed a belief in how they were playing, we were a threat right up until the end. When you consider where we are, we have come up from the Championship. I think we’ve progressed in this first period of games.

“We came up against a fully loaded squad. Eight of the boys who started, played for us last year at the Championship. I just thought they showed real personality in how they played.

“The last goal changes the feel slightly but it shouldn’t do in terms of how we performed.”

articles.title: Ronaldo handed 30-day suspension for Portugal walkout
articles.summary: Ronaldo will reportedly be available for selection next month.
articles.content:
Ronaldo handed 30-day suspension for Portugal walkout

Ronaldo will reportedly be available for selection next month.

Last Update:

The Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) has suspended Cristiano Ronaldo for 30 days after leaving the national team camp during the recent international window.

Ronaldo left the squad early amid a dispute with Jorge Jesus stemming from the coach’s decision not to bring him as a substitute in Portugal‘s UEFA Nations League win in Norway.

The former Manchester United and Real Madrid star subsequently released a lengthy statement detailing the reasons behind his actions.

Ronaldo, who accused Jesus of breaking his word, apologised for leaving his team-mates and for failing to walk over to the travelling fans following the game against Norway. The 41-year-old added that he remained available for selection for the national team, dispelling talk of retirement, and said he would accept any punishment for his decision.

The FPF disciplinary council’s non-professional section found Ronaldo to have intentionally committed an offence in breach of Article 160(1) ‌of the federation’s disciplinary regulations.

Proceedings against Ronaldo were opened on October 9 and on Monday the disciplinary council said it had upheld the original charge.

The ruling did not state the matches or activities the suspension would cover. It also did not specify if time served under a provisional suspension would count towards the 30-day ban.

Ronaldo was also fined €255 (£215), but reports in the Portuguese media have claimed he will be available for selection during the November international break.

Portugal beat Denmark and won a return meeting with Norway in Porto in Ronaldo’s self-imposed absence.

Having already clinched qualification for the Nations League quarter-finals, Portugal host Denmark on November 14 before rounding off their group stage campaign with a trip to Wales three days later.

articles.title: Liverpool to be ‘patient’ with Szoboszlai following latest injury
articles.summary: The Reds suffered two injury blows in their victory over Brentford.
articles.content:
Liverpool to be ‘patient’ with Szoboszlai following latest injury

The Reds suffered two injury blows in their victory over Brentford.

Last Update:

Andoni Iraola indicated Dominik Szoboszlai will not be out for a long time but cautioned Liverpool will need to be patient with the injury that forced him off against Brentford.

Having missed the 3-0 defeat to Manchester City with a hamstring issue and then sat out the Champions League victory over LASK Linz before making his return in West London.

However, a thigh issue led to Szoboszlai being substituted just after the half-hour mark, though Liverpool were still able to come from behind to claim a 2-1 victory.

Liverpool also saw right-back Jeremie Frimpong suffer a thigh injury. Speaking ahead of Tuesday’s Champions League clash with Villarreal, Iraola was more positive on Szoboszlai, with Frimpong seemingly facing a longer lay-off.

“I think they are different circumstances,” Iraola said.

“Jeremie Frimpong is obviously a new muscle injury and it happened, I think, in the second or third minute he was playing, difficult to predict and we will have to wait until he recovers.

“But it’s going to be difficult, I think, before the [November international] break. We will try but it’s going to be difficult to have him.

“Dom Szoboszlai is different. It’s not a new injury, I think it’s in the same place it was probably last week. He hasn’t worsened the injury but probably we have to be a little bit more patient until he recovers fully.

“But it’s not like something now where he has to wait a lot of time to come back, he is more or less in the same situation he was last week.

“But we need more patience with him, but I appreciate the effort he did the other day, to be available, to want to contribute in a very difficult game that you know is going to be very physical – [against] one of the most physical teams, Brentford.

“And to put himself in front and to want to play speaks very well about him, yes.”

articles.title: BREAKING: Manchester City star Semenyo ruled out for eight weeks
articles.summary: Antoine Semenyo may not play again in 2026 due to a lower leg injury, according to Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca
articles.content:
BREAKING: Manchester City star Semenyo ruled out for eight weeks

Antoine Semenyo may not play again in 2026 due to a lower leg injury, according to Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca

Last Update:

Manchester City winger Antoine Semenyo has been ruled out for eight weeks, Enzo Maresca has confirmed.

Semenyo was left on the bench for Saturday’s 3-2 win at home to Ipswich but came on, replacing Jeremy Doku, with 13 minutes to go only to suffer a lower leg problem.

Maresca revealed the issue was not muscular and confirmed the Ghana international is set for a lengthy spell on the sidelines.

Speaking ahead of Tuesday night’s home game with AEK Athens in the Champions League, the City boss said: “In the first moment we expected an even worse injury, so we were more worried, but after yesterday’s scan we feel much better because it is not so big like we expected.

“It could be eight weeks. So now in the moment, the most important thing for him is to recover and also when he is back, probably around December, we will have a new player in terms of energy.

“It is a collateral [lower leg injury], something like this. It is not muscle, not a muscle problem.”

Semenyo blow for City and Haaland

The setback is not ideal for Maresca as he wrestles with a way of trying to give star striker Erling Haaland a rest. Haaland is also struggling for full fitness and is touch and go for the AEK game.

Semenyo is one of the few players in the City squad that can play up front but Maresca says he has other options.

“First of all to lose Antonine or any player for us, it is not good,” he added.

“Then in terms of Erling [Haaland], we said that we can use Antoine as a nine but also we have different players that we are going to try and find new solutions.

“We will see. At the moment it is Erling, why do we need to think about a different nine when Erling is there?

“Then, if something happens, we need a different plan or a different nine. There is also the chance that he can be available tomorrow. We’ll see.”

We need to win games – City boss Maresca

City are in the middle of a frenetic run of games but Maresca insisted he would not take AEK lightly.

He said: “It is a huge game, tomorrow for us. It is a Champions League game, unfortunately we lost the last one, we need to win games and we are going to try to win the game with our best players in this moment.”

Maresca had a brief spell in Greek football, as a player with Olympiacos in the 2009/10 season.

“It is a Champions League game, different competition but the ambition has to be the same, try to win games and again,” he said. “I had one year experience there [in Greece]. As I said a few conferences ago, it is nice because it is very warm, every game, at home, away, but it was a good experience.”

articles.title: Are you Arsene in disguise? Mourinho follows old rival in insisting he did not see Guler elbow in Real Madrid win
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho insists he has not seen the incident in which Real Madrid midfielder Arda Güler elbowed Sevilla's Peque Fernandez
articles.content:
Are you Arsene in disguise? Mourinho follows old rival in insisting he did not see Guler elbow in Real Madrid win

Jose Mourinho insists he has not seen the incident in which Real Madrid midfielder Arda Güler elbowed Sevilla's Peque Fernandez

Last Update:

Jose Mourinho took a leaf out of old sparring partner Arsene Wenger’s playbook by insisting he hadn’t seen the incident that should have resulted in a red card for Real Madrid midfielder Arda Guler last night.

Guler threw his elbow into the face of Sevilla midfielder Peque Fernandez midway through the first half of the clash at the Santiago Bernabeu.

Referee Mateo Busquets Ferrer did not see the coming-together while VAR Guillermo Cuadra Fernandez opted against taking any action.

To make matters worse for the visitors, Guler then opened the scoring with a lovely strike that paved the way for Madrid to cruise to a 4-1 win and move back within six points of leaders Barcelona ahead of next weekend’s Clasico.

I have not seen Guler elbow – Real Madrid boss Mourinho

Sevilla were outraged with boss Luis García Plaza expressing his disappointment but Mourinho, who has reopened his crusade against Spanish referees since returning to Madrid over the summer, claimed not to have seen a good enough angle of the clash.

He said: ”No-one has managed to make me see what they say has happened. I don’t have the pictures and I haven’t been able to see it. I have asked for images from the TV and the analysts and I have not been able to see any image of the things they are talking about and that have bothered Sevilla.

“I say it in all honesty. If one day something happens that I think has benefited us, I will not have any kind of problem going out and saying that but I think the opposite will happen to us many times because it is the natural trend of things.

“If from here to the Clasico, there is any image, I would like to see it.”

Wenger became well known for claiming he did not see any incident that could have benefited Arsenal during his time in the Premier League. The Frenchman had a difficult relationship with Mourinho with the then Chelsea boss accusing of him being a “voyeur” and a “specialist in failure”.

The row boiled over in 2014 when they a physical confrontation during a game at Stamford Bridge.

articles.title: Sevilla boss claims Real Madrid star Guler escaped red card to keep title race close ahead of Clasico
articles.summary: Sevilla were furious that Arda Güler escaped a red card last night as they were beaten 4-1 at the Bernabeu by Real Madrid
articles.content:
Sevilla boss claims Real Madrid star Guler escaped red card to keep title race close ahead of Clasico

Sevilla were furious that Arda Güler escaped a red card last night as they were beaten 4-1 at the Bernabeu by Real Madrid

Last Update:

Sevilla boss Luis Garcia Plaza claimed Arda Guler escaped a red card last night because La Liga wanted Real Madrid to win to close the gap on Barcelona before next week’s Clasico.

Garcia Plaza’s side lost 4-1 at the Santiago Bernabeu – a result that enabled Madrid to move within six points of Barca – but the match was shrouded in controversy with Guler escaping what seemed an obvious red card for elbowing Peque Fernandez as the pair jostled midway through the first half.

Referee Mateo Busquets Ferrer did not see the incident while VAR Guillermo Cuadra Fernandez opted against taking any action. The flashpoint caused a melee in which Madrid’s Dean Huijsen and Sevilla captain Felix Correia were both booked.

Real Madrid benefit from lax refereeing

To make matters worse for Sevilla, Guler then scored the opener for Madrid shortly afterwards and from there the home side cruised with Kylian Mbappe scoring twice and Yan Diomande adding another. Manu Bueno pulled one back for the visitors but they felt a clear sense of injustice after the game.

Garcia Plaza said: “A game is 11 against 11, but we have been deprived of playing 11 against 10. In the league sometimes you play games with a greater or lesser number and today it was our turn to play with more.

“We have to play 11 against 10 from the 25th minute. It’s incredible. It’s the summary of the game, we don’t know what would have happened.”

García Plaza claims Clasico considerations influenced decision-making

Asked why the VAR had not intervened, Garcia Plaza added: “I don’t know. Maybe because they [Madrid] would go nine points behind Barca ahead of the Clasico if we win? You should talk to the VAR more than the referee, who may not have seen it. With Barça, Madrid and Atlético there are many more cameras on the field, hence for me it is one more VAR view. It’s a very clear foul.”

Sevilla’s complaints came just 24 hours after Real Betis boss Manuel Pellegrini outlined his frustrations at what he perceived as a number of decisions that went in favour of Barcelona on Saturday night as the league leaders won 5-2 at La Cartuja.

And while Madrid and Barca frequently engage in verbal sparring regarding the standard of refereeing in Spain, Garcia Plaza highlighted the fact that, in his opinion, they are among the two clubs that benefit most.

He said: ”Those who complain the most are the ones who have the least to complain about: Madrid, Barça and Atlético. I’ve been in this for a long time and it’s always the same story.”

articles.title: Madueke hails Arsenal’s ‘absurd’ strength in depth after grabbing late winner at Nottingham Forest
articles.summary: Noni Madueke came off the bench to grab a late winner as Arsenal won at Nottingham Forest this afternoon
articles.content:
Madueke hails Arsenal’s ‘absurd’ strength in depth after grabbing late winner at Nottingham Forest

Noni Madueke came off the bench to grab a late winner as Arsenal won at Nottingham Forest this afternoon

Last Update:

Noni Madueke hailed the “absurd’ strength of Arsenal’s squad after he came off the bench to grab the winner at Nottingham Forest this afternoon.

Madueke started among the substitutes but his introduction at half-time for the ineffective Eberechi Eze brought some pep to the Gunners attack and it was no surprise that he conjured up the only goal of a largely dismal affair.

The former Chelsea man cut in from the left with 10 minutes to go and fired in a shot that took a deflection off the unfortunate Jair Cunha and flew past Matz Sels. It was Arsenal’s only shot on target.

Forest twice came close to an equaliser in injury time through Murillo and Liam Delap but Arsenal held on to move back up to second, three points behind leaders Manchester City.

Madueke told BBC MOTD: “If you look at the quality of our starting XI and bench it’s absurd so we know that we’re going to start some and finish some and for me it’s the same mentality every time. I just want to create or score.

“It’s an amazing feeling [to score] but I feel better about the win. We have elite players, all 20-something players are elite and of the highest level. Great to have that type of competition. You know on the bench you’re ready to have an impact.

“I had beaten him [his marker] on the outside a couple of times. I thought come inside and leather it.”

Forest made life difficult for Arsenal – Madueke

Forest slipped into the relegation zone this weekend but Madueke was relieved to have come away with three points after two successive goalless draws at the City Ground.

He added: ”They make it so difficult for you. It was a tough game. We’re really happy all together. We showed grit and determination and showed a champion spirit. At times, maybe last year, this game might not have gone for us in the end. We have the extra belief and mentality.”

Arteta was equally pleased his players stuck to their task despite being largely under-par.

“We had to earn it until the last second,” he said. “They are a well-coached team and hard to break down. We had to take risks, they are a dangerous team. We had to manage the emotional part really well. We stayed focused and the finishers made a huge impact.

“Sometimes you can get frustrated with teams who are difficult to break down. First half we didn’t have a shot on target and that’s something we discussed. We had another two big ones in the second half but the only one on target we had was a little deflection and it’s in.”

It was the third win in eight days for Arsenal after beating Leeds and Lille.

“Some of them played three days ago and some of them will start the next game and they know that everyone has to be at it,” said Arteta when asked about the players at his disposal. “If you are needed after 60 minutes, 45 minutes and sometimes two minutes – we have a squad now that can deliver in moments and we have to use that.

“Noni [Madueke], Jurrien [Timber], Mikel [Merino] were brilliant when they came on and Viktor [Gyokeres] really changed the game – all of them did and that’s what we need. Noni obviously the highlight because he scored the goal and that’s the difference.”

Murillo backs Glasner to turn it round despite Arsenal setback

Despite sitting 18th in the table, Murillo was confident the situation will improve for Forest under Oliver Glasner.

He said: “We have a good manager and I think we are still getting his ideas. We changed everything in our system this season. It is difficult but after three or four months we keep improving and I think we are close to reaching our best.

“We have a very good team, experienced players as well. Now we keep going because we know how tough the Premier League is.”

articles.summary: Nottingham Forest were keeping Arsenal at arm's length during the first half hour at the City Ground this afternoon
articles.content:
Gabriel comes closest as Arsenal struggle to break down Nottingham Forest in turgid encounter

Nottingham Forest were keeping Arsenal at arm's length during the first half hour at the City Ground this afternoon

Last Update:

Arsenal struggled to hit top gear in a disappointing first half against Nottingham Forest this afternoon.

The Gunners failed to register a shot on target in a forgettable opening 45 minutes despite having the bulk of the possession at the City Ground.

The visitors, who were hoping to close the gap to Premier League leaders Manchester City back to three points, offered very little going forward with Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze creating little.

FOLLOW THE GAME LIVE HERE…

Forest were without key midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White due to injury but still created the first half-chance with Dan Ndoye firing a shot into the sidenetting after 20 minutes.

Arsenal responded by almost going ahead from a corner seven minutes later. Forest failed to clear Saka’s right-wing delivery, enabling Gabriel to attempt an audacious back heel that appeared to be heading in before hitting defensive partner Ezri Konsa and Forest got the ball clear.

Arsenal had another opportunity seven minutes before the break. Saka won a free-kick with a shocking dive under minimal contact from Xaver Schlager and Declan Rice’s whipped delivery was headed over by Havertz when he arguably should’ve done better.

Havertz then shot into the side netting from a tight angle as Arsenal cranked up the pressure approaching half-time.

articles.title: Leeds point ‘a step forward’ for Man Utd says Carrick
articles.summary: It's the worst start to a league season for 40 years at Old Trafford
articles.content:
Leeds point ‘a step forward’ for Man Utd says Carrick

It's the worst start to a league season for 40 years at Old Trafford

Last Update:

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said his side are making progress after they were held to a 1-1 draw at rivals Leeds in the Premier League.

Bryan Mbeumo’s first-half opener was cancelled out by Dominic Calvert-Lewin after the break to leave United on seven points from seven games.

It’s their worst start to a season since 1986 – when Sir Alex Ferguson arrived at Old Trafford – but Carrick was pleased with the performance.

He said: “In little moments and spells we played some really good football. It’s a tough place to come.

“With the results we’ve had we weren’t quite flowing but there’s enough in there to take from it. We had to work for it. I was proud of the boys for the way they went about it in difficult circumstances. A point is a point. It is a step forward for us.

“It was a tense game, a tight game. It was kind of one of those games which could have gone both ways so we take the point and move on.”

Carrick started Lisandro Martinez despite his explosive criticism in midweek following the defeat to Atletico Madrid – but he came off at the break.

The visitors were more intense and organised, and Carrick was pleased with the togetherness shown by his under-fire players.

He said: “You’re looking at the togetherness, the spirit, the unit. I don’t doubt that within the group and they’ve shown that even more so in the last two days. They showed it today.

“It is clear they want to do well. They are a really tight group. Things haven’t gone our way. Some of it is to do with us. Some of it is a bit here and there and luck in moments.” The way that we went about it today gives me a lot of belief in us moving forward that we are a strong group and if we build on that with the quality we have got in the group already we will win football matches.”

Leeds United boss Daniel Farke felt his team deserved to win.

Leeds had five shots on target in a spirited display and end the weekend in seventh place in the table.

Farke told Sky Sports: “We are slightly disappointed it is just a point. Overall, I felt it was not necessary to be losing at half time but it is still Manchester United.

“Second half, we got the equaliser, we should have kept up the dominance, too many strikes went over the crossbar but it was overall a solid performance. We should have won the game but we move on.

“We took it as a compliment that we have done many things right over the last month if we were seen as favourites against Manchester Untiedbut we have earned this. We wanted to prove the comments right.

“We were the dominant side but we couldn’t capitalise as we lacked quality in and around the box.”

Operating as the orchestrator of an attack that has already racked up 18 goals, Gross also monopolises penalties, corners, and attacking free-kicks, making him a constant threat against an out-of-sorts Palace defence that regularly struggles against deliveries from wide areas.

Elsewhere, Elland Road sets the stage for a fiery Roses rivalry, and backing both teams to score when Leeds United host Manchester United looks like the ideal foundation for a weekend double.

Leeds rarely draw a blank in front of a raucous home crowd and have found the net with consistency all season, while Michael Carrick’s side remain fragile at the back having managed just one victory in six league outings. With United languishing in 14th place yet still boasting genuine transitional firepower on the break, this historic fixture has all the ingredients of an open, end-to-end clash where clean sheets will be hard to come by.

articles.title: ‘He never ceases to amaze’: Gonzalez backs Messi for 1,000 goals after Atlanta masterclass
articles.summary: The Argentina legend was at it again for Inter Miami
articles.content:
‘He never ceases to amaze’: Gonzalez backs Messi for 1,000 goals after Atlanta masterclass

The Argentina legend was at it again for Inter Miami

Last Update:

Inter Miami head coach Kily Gonzalez backed Lionel Messi to reach 1,000 career goals following another match-winning masterclass in the win at Atlanta.

Messi took centre stage at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, producing a devastating four-minute blitz in the second half to score twice after earlier register an assist. The result solidifies Miami’s grip on second place in the Eastern Conference, while leaving the hosts languishing down in 14th spot.

Former Argentina winger Gonzalez admitted he still finds it difficult to process what the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner continues to produce well into his late thirties.

“He never ceases to amaze the world,” González said. “I mean, I honestly can’t believe that a guy like him, at 39 years old, is doing what he’s doing.

“And what makes me happiest is seeing that he’s truly happy. Because he’s happy, he gives everything he has. He enjoys himself and feels right at home.”

The Miami boss was equally keen to highlight how the former Argentina captain’s relentless hunger continues to elevate everyone around him.

“As I always say, he pushes us to be better every single day,” Gonzalez said.

“It’s an immense joy to have him here. Every time I see him, he brings a smile to my face. I’m still constantly amazed by him.”

Following a cagey opening period, Miami broke the deadlock right on the stroke of halftime through German Berterame, who finished neatly after intricate build-up play involving both Messi and Luis Suarez.

Atlanta United FC

Inter Miami

Messi then took full control of the contest early in the second half. On 56 minutes, he traded a slick one-two with Berterame before dancing past his marker to roll a composed finish into the bottom corner.

Just four minutes later, Suarez turned provider with a through ball on the counter, allowing Messi to surge clear and place an emphatic strike beyond Lucas Hoyos.

Atlanta snatched a late consolation when Fafa Picault converted from the penalty spot.

The double elevated Messi’s extraordinary career tally to 936 goals, leaving a historic four-figure total firmly within sight. When asked if the forward can realistically breach the 1,000-goal barrier before hanging up his boots, Gonzalez expressed total faith in his talisman.

“Yes, I believe he’ll reach 1,000 goals,” he said.

“I have faith in that. I know he will, because he loves a challenge, he sets challenges for himself and since he’s already achieved everything else, this will be no exception.”

Messi now has 25 league goals for the campaign.

articles.title: Martinez back for Chelsea ‘in a few weeks’ after operation
articles.summary: The Chelsea number one was concussed after a nasty clash of heads
articles.content:
Martinez back for Chelsea ‘in a few weeks’ after operation

The Chelsea number one was concussed after a nasty clash of heads

Last Update:

Chelsea goalkeeper Emi Martinez says he expects to be “back in a few weeks” after undergoing surgery following a severe clash of heads on Saturday.

The shot-stopper was involved in a sickening collision with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite as both players challenged for a cross during the second half at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

The match was halted for over eight minutes while medical personnel attended to Martinez on the pitch.

The World Cup winner was carefully immobilised, stretchered off the field, and taken directly to a waiting ambulance before being transported to a local hospital for emergency evaluation and subsequent surgery. Belgian youngster Mike Penders came on to replace him in goal, with the lengthy stoppage contributing to 11 minutes of added time.

Taking to Instagram on Sunday, Martinez moved quickly to reassure supporters, sharing a photo from his hospital bed with an optimistic message:

“Thank you for all the messages, the operation went well. We’ll be back in a few weeks.”

The injury cast a shadow over an otherwise clinical away performance from the Blues, who ran out 2-0 winners to snap Everton’s unbeaten start to the Premier League campaign.

Before his premature exit, Martinez had played a key role in repelling David Moyes’ side, including producing a sharp first-half save to tip Jack Grealish’s effort over the crossbar.

The collective defensive effort preserved Chelsea’s first Premier League clean sheet in nine months – halting a 22-game run without a league shutout and lifting the Blues up into fourth in the table.

While the three points provided plenty of reason for optimism, all eyes now turn to Martinez’s road to recovery over the coming weeks.

articles.title: Foden pleased to be off the mark as Manchester City maintain perfect Premier League record against plucky Ipswich
articles.summary: Phil Foden made an impressive return from suspension as Manchester City edged out Ipswich at the Etihad
articles.content:
Foden pleased to be off the mark as Manchester City maintain perfect Premier League record against plucky Ipswich

Phil Foden made an impressive return from suspension as Manchester City edged out Ipswich at the Etihad

Last Update:

Phil Foden was delighted to have scored his first Premier League goal since December as Manchester City maintained their 100% record in the Premier League with a nervy victory over Ipswich.

The England midfielder was making his first league appearance since his red card in the Manchester derby and capped a good performance with the opener as City won 3-2.

City goal was a matter of time – Foden

Foden told BBC Match of the Day: “Amazing feeling. Obviously I’ve missed a few big chances this season, I knew it would be a matter of time before it came. Enzo [Maresca] said that I would score today, so thanks to him. I think he gave me the good luck that I needed so I am obviously delighted to help the team. Today was just about getting the three points because now it puts us in a really good position.

“It gives you a lot of confidence, it makes us go out there and want to express yourself and give back to the manager. Today, I just tried to do that as best as I could.”

Foden struck from Jeremy Doku’s delivery to put City ahead, only for Ipswich to equalise when Daizen Maeda raced into the box and beat Gianluigi Donnarumma in clinical fashion as part of an incisive move.

Erling Haaland headed in Mateo Kovacic’s cross via grounded goalkeeper Christian Walton to restore City’s lead at half-time and produced a composed touch and finish from Iliman Ndiaye’s pass to add to their advantage during the second period.

A Video Assistant Referee offside decision denied Haaland a third when the Norway striker fired in seconds after Ndiaye hit the crossbar, with Zian Flemming then converting a penalty for a foul by Marc Guehi on Abdul Fatawu.

“It wasn’t pretty, I think they played a really good game,” added Foden. “They pressed us high and made it really difficult for us. Sometimes, they are not going to be pretty in the Premier League. Every team is so good now and it’s always going to be a big challenge. To come out with the three points, that was the main thing. Overall, we’re really happy.”

Latest updated Premier League table

Premier League 2026

England

O’Neil proud of plucky Ipswich

Ipswich can also take plenty from the game with boss Gary O’Neill delighted with their display.

He told Sky Sports: “Really proud of the group. I think they had a go today. There’s bits in it that we could have done better. The second goal I’m really disappointed with because it is something we had covered. When I say covered, I really mean covered. That disappointed me after we got back in it.

“Towards the end, we showed a little bit too much excitement and not enough quality. We wasted some fantastic opportunities, but really proud of the group. To stand at the front and be able to lead a team with that endeavour and that adventure and the support we have, I’m really proud because it really is an excellent group.

“We came here looking for points and I really thought we could have got that. We didn’t and that is disappointing but whether it be a couple of mistakes from us like for the goal, whether it be the three offsides that weren’t offside that were given against us which were mad, you only get six attacks at the Etihad so to lose three of them just kill your momentum. You’ve got VAR, just let it go.”

articles.title: Relieved Arbeloa praises his Fulham team after deserved win over slumping Hull
articles.summary: Alex Iwobi scored the only goal as Fulham earned their first Premier League win of the season by beating Hull at Craven Cottage
articles.content:
Relieved Arbeloa praises his Fulham team after deserved win over slumping Hull

Alex Iwobi scored the only goal as Fulham earned their first Premier League win of the season by beating Hull at Craven Cottage

Last Update:

Alvaro Arbeloa believes Fulham finally got what they deserved after Alex Iwobi’s first-half goal was enough to beat Hull and secure their first Premier League victory of the season.

The Cottagers started the day as one of three winless teams in the top-flight – Bournemouth and Tottenham the others – but got off the mark to move out of the bottom three.

Iwobi’s goal came from some poor Hull defending with the Tigers twice failing to clear their lines, enabling the former Everton midfielder to shoot past Konstantinos Tzolakis, via a deflection off Lucas Herrington.

Fulham were good value for the win with the only blemish coming late on when Ryan Sessegnon was sent-off for a poor challenge on Robinio Vaz.

Match Statistics

Arbeloa – Fulham win was overdue

The victory eases the pressure on boss Arbeloa but he felt his side were worthy winners.

He told BBC Match of the Day: “I am very happy, especially for the supporters, they deserve this win, for the players, they were looking for this victory and have been working so hard. We deserved it in other matches, but we couldn’t get it; today was finally the day.

“We were having the same feeling as other matches, when we were controlling the game for long spells and having good chances but didn’t score. Our rivals punish our mistakes or take their chances, but today we were brilliant for 90 minutes. We controlled the game, had many chances and didn’t concede any clear chances to Hull, a very good team. They are tough to beat. We need to keep going and keep improving.

“We have so many players with talent who can score. They will have chances. Players from the bench will be so important for us too. We have many chances and we need to try to take them.”

Fulham go to Coventry next weekend before facing Crystal Palace in the EFL Cup.

“It’s a massive week because we have Coventry, then Palace,” said Arbeloa. “It won’t be easy, but we know how we need to play and compete, we have to be competitive in this league.”

Premier League 2026

England

Fulham were much better than us – Hull boss Jakirovic

Hull defied expectations with a strong start to the season following promotion but have now failed to win any of their last five in the Premier League.

And boss Sergej Jakirovic had no arguments with the result. He said: “It’s easy to analyse this game; we were out of everything. Fulham were much better than us, in and out of possession, first and second balls, duels. It was men against boys. We didn’t show anything today. But we cannot change anything now.

“The performances of Fulham have been good; they should have more points. We knew it would be tough today. We were completely out of it.

“It was very frustrating, maybe we had some situations around the box but made wrong decisions. They were much more aggressive than us and could have scored more.”

articles.title: Man City boss Maresca reveals Pep Guardiola meeting: ‘We were talking’
articles.summary: City's perfect start ended on Champions League Matchday 2
articles.content:
Man City boss Maresca reveals Pep Guardiola meeting: ‘We were talking’

City's perfect start ended on Champions League Matchday 2

Last Update:

Enzo Maresca has said Manchester City’s Etihad Stadium is Pep Guardiola’s “house” and described his predecessor as “very positive” when the pair met after the Cityzens lost at home to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Guardiola, who left City after 10 years at the end of last season, made his first appearance at the stadium since the club was found guilty of 114 breaches of Premier League rules, a verdict against which they have appealed.

“I saw him after the game,” said Maresca, who had a brief spell as Guardiola’s assistant from June 2022 before joining Leicester City the following year.

“We were talking about the game. He was, first of all, very happy to be at the stadium, and then said very positive about things he had seen during the game.

“I said before the game that I think it was great also for the fans to see him at the stadium. This will always be his house.”

Man City charges: What has Pep Guardiola said?

Guardiola appeared to address City fans after the Premier League announced the ruling in September.

“Let me be clear,” said the City icon. “We will get through this together. I love you all.”

In his most recent public comments about the charges, Guardiola backed club owners City Football Group, for whom he remains a global ambassador.

“I spoke with them and trust how they behave and how they did,” the Spaniard said in May, via BBC Sport. “What happened, happened.”

Maresca, who has guided City three points clear at the top of the table by winning his first six league matches in charge, reiterated his trust in the group in his remarks before City host 10th-placed Ipswich Town on Saturday.

Pep Guardiola: Man City trophies

City became the dominant force in English football for much of Guardiola’s reign, with many crediting the former Barcelona and Bayern Munich manager with transforming the English game because of his possession-heavy passing style.

Here are the trophies he won with the club.

Enzo Maresca praises Manchester City fans’ bananas

Inflatable bananas were on display around the stadium during City’s 4-2 defeat to the European holders, Maresca’s team falling short of a second-half comeback after conceding three goals without reply before the break.

The tradition among City fans dates to the late 1980s and Maresca suggested he could take one of the inflatables home after the game against Town.

“Very nice,” the Italian said of the decorations. “I didn’t know the story behind the bananas. I hope [against Town] I can see many bananas in the stadium.

“It creates a nice environment for the fans and everyone who is in the stadium.”

Enzo Fernandez: Manchester City signing ‘nice’

City bought midfielder Enzo Fernandez from Maresca’s former club, Chelsea, for a Premier League record-equaling £125 million in September and the Argentina international was involved in a bizarre incident against PSG when he pushed referee Sven Jablonski over from behind.

The official did not appear to deem the shove intentional and Maresca defended the 25-year-old when a reporter suggested Fernandez has shown a fiery temper in the past.

“It’s just a random moment,” said Maresca, adding that Fernandez was “not even thinking” of acting maliciously. “It was a bit funny.

“He’s a nice person. He has a big heart [and is] polite, professional. Sometimes the image from outside is completely different from the reality.

“He’s a top guy and, first of all, he’s a very nice person. Nice family, mama, dad, wife, kids. I know all of them. That’s why. There’s no doubt about that.”
